s646ad3cf3c.summary: Researchers propose allocating perceptual detail to past agent interactions based on resolution, treating resolution as a form of attention for agent memory.
s646ad3cf3c.why: Varying the granularity of stored memories offers a possible way to manage memory cost in long-horizon agents.

sa885ef85ff.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
sa885ef85ff.description: arXiv:2611.24436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthetic polysomnography (PSG) data has great potential in healthcare applications, for example in substituting real data that is sensitive and challenging to collect. Previous research on synthetic PSG data has been largely focused on short segments of individual signals, overlooking the inter-signal dynamics related to sleep disorders. In this study, we developed a generative adversarial network (PSG-GAN) for co-synthesizing longer segments of multiple PSG signals with diverse and complex characteristics typical of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The synthetic signals appeared realistic, and the electroencephalography and electrooculography band powers were similarly distributed across sleep stages. Moreover, the PSG-GAN learned to mirror s
sa885ef85ff.summary: PSG-GAN is a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes longer multi-signal polysomnography segments showing obstructive sleep apnea characteristics.
sa885ef85ff.why: Synthetic multi-signal medical data could help teams train models where real patient data is sensitive or scarce.

sa6b3b1e011.title: Study and Improvement of Search Algorithms in Stochastic Perfect-Information
sa6b3b1e011.description: arXiv:2611.24486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we generalize Unbounded Minimax, the state- of-the-art search algorithm for deterministic zero-sum two- player games with perfect information to the framework of stochastic zero-sum two-player games with perfect informa- tion. We experimentally show that this generalized algorithm achieves better performance than the main stochastic search algorithms.
sa6b3b1e011.summary: The authors generalize Unbounded Minimax to stochastic zero-sum two-player perfect-information games and report better performance than main stochastic search algorithms.

s056e6e1e21.title: The Largest Tractable Subclass of Multi-Scale Allen Temporal Reasoning
s056e6e1e21.description: arXiv:2611.24498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model for temporal reasoning over multi-scale intervals. We show that this model yields a complete reasoning framework and exhibits other particularly interesting properties. Furthermore, we identify the maximal tractable subalgebra for this model, as well as for the other complete model, in the qualitative scales context, which exhibits weaker properties but whose results can be derived by transfer from our new model.
s056e6e1e21.summary: The paper proposes a new model for temporal reasoning over multi-scale intervals and identifies its maximal tractable subalgebra.

s0073f7aaf9.title: ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation
s0073f7aaf9.description: arXiv:2611.24517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based artificial societies exhibit rich behavior but often lack scientific grounding: personas and environments are assumed, interaction networks are synthetic, and simulators are generated as free-form code, making results difficult to tie to real populations and sensitive to the backbone model. We argue that simulated worlds should be sampled from observed data, while simulation logic should be implemented by composing operations from a shared, task-independent vocabulary. In this paper, we introduce ABSClaw, a zero-code agent that compiles natural-language requests into executable, reality-grounded social simulations. ABSClaw grounds who acts, where they act, and with whom they interact in survey and census data, geospatial sources, an
s0073f7aaf9.summary: ABSClaw is a zero-code agent that builds LLM-based social simulations from observed data, composing operations from a shared task-independent vocabulary.
s0073f7aaf9.why: Grounding simulated societies in real data rather than assumed personas could make LLM simulation results more defensible for research use.

s92cee862e3.title: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
s92cee862e3.description: arXiv:2611.24552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal knowledge graph reasoning (MKGR) aims to infer missing facts by jointly exploiting relational structures, textual descriptions, and visual evidence. Existing embedding-based methods effectively capture graph topology, but their fixed multimodal representations are less effective for query-specific fine-grained semantic reasoning, while generation-based methods are vulnerable to noisy retrieval and may produce invalid entities. To address these challenges, we propose NaviGATE, a noise-aware generative framework for MKGR. NaviGATE first aligns graph-derived structural representations with textual semantics, then performs structure-aware internal knowledge activation by fine-tuning the multimodal language model with multimodal entity
s92cee862e3.summary: NaviGATE is a noise-aware generative framework for multimodal knowledge graph reasoning that combines relational structure, text and visual evidence.

sa624ef0611.title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
sa624ef0611.description: arXiv:2611.24568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current command and control (C2) platforms lack integrated simulation capabilities that would allow commanders to dynamically explore courses of action (COAs) during live operations. This paper presents ongoing research and contributions to the development of AGAMOTTO (Advanced Guidance and Analytics for Military Operations, Tactical Threats, and Outcomes) as part of the overarching NGC2 program, which advances the Army's efforts to modernize C2 systems, such as the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK). The paper outlines the current design, preliminary findings, and the remaining research tasks, with an emphasis on how the completed work will support tactical decision-making in future time-constrained environments. While the full system is still under
sa624ef0611.summary: AGAMOTTO is a research framework that adds simulation to military command-and-control platforms so commanders can evaluate courses of action during operations.
sa624ef0611.why: It shows AI-enabled simulation being integrated into live C2 tooling, relevant to defense-software builders, though details are preliminary.

s38c4c8e925.title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code
s38c4c8e925.description: arXiv:2611.24590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-trained models can read screens and reason about games, yet on an unfamiliar game, an agent still has to learn to play. We ask how an agent can self-improve on such a game from a few of its own attempts, in real-time visual games where the agent sees only the screen and the game keeps running while the agent thinks. We study two kinds of policy that can carry this improvement. In model as policy, a model selects actions during play; we adapt real-time chunking so that committed actions keep executing while the model reasons, and train a 2B controller for this interface. In code as policy, a model writes, tests, and revises a program between attempts, and the program acts during play. Across 170 GameWorld tasks, with at most eight one-minu
s38c4c8e925.summary: Researchers study how agents can self-improve in real-time visual games from their own attempts, using model-as-policy and code-based policy approaches.
s38c4c8e925.why: Real-time action execution while the model reasons is a concrete design pattern for latency-sensitive agent systems.

sf02aea4c38.title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
sf02aea4c38.description: arXiv:2611.24619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes important for detecting unsafe or unintended actions. Activation probes offer an efficient approach, but existing methods face trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, and computational overhead. Probes on raw activations lack interpretable inputs, whereas sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes use interpretable features but often rely on additive classifiers and large SAE encoders, limiting interpretability and increasing memory overhead. We introduce GateWatch, a compact, interpretable classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as an explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features. We explore three ap
sf02aea4c38.summary: GateWatch proposes low-overhead LLM activation monitoring using Boolean circuits over interpretable features instead of additive classifiers.
sf02aea4c38.why: Cheaper, more interpretable runtime monitors for unsafe LLM behavior could help teams deploy safety checks with less compute overhead.

s0bd98442b5.title: Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models
s0bd98442b5.description: arXiv:2611.24650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels.We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2,000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a
s0bd98442b5.summary: Researchers apply self-rewarded reinforcement learning to Mistral-7B so small medical language models produce better-structured clinical explanations.
s0bd98442b5.why: On-premises small models that give structured medical explanations could suit privacy-sensitive clinical deployments, though results are not given here.

sab3f7ca9c8.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
sab3f7ca9c8.description: arXiv:2611.24669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness
sab3f7ca9c8.summary: Researchers introduced Movie2Game-Bench, a benchmark evaluating film-to-game adaptations beyond playability, using 22 films, 658 source-specific items, and GUI model playtesting.
sab3f7ca9c8.why: It offers a structured way to measure whether games preserve source content and realize it interactively, not just whether they are playable.

sb771dc21ca.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
sb771dc21ca.description: arXiv:2611.24697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for
sb771dc21ca.summary: Researchers propose a reverse-to-forward curriculum with advantage decomposition to train LLM agents on long-horizon tasks with sparse terminal rewards.
sb771dc21ca.why: It targets credit assignment and exploration problems that make reinforcement learning for long-horizon LLM agents hard.

s60fb031f69.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
s60fb031f69.description: arXiv:2611.24708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures. What, then, makes good experience for a WAM? We show that experience is valuable only in use: its value depends not on whether the source rollout succeeded but on what is stored, when it is used, and where it enters the policy. We therefore propose F$^3$, which makes these three decisions with Form, Fit, and Fusion. Form compresses successful and failed rollouts alike into short, verified operation records; Fit teaches the policy to read a record and to predict when it helps; Fusion
s60fb031f69.summary: Researchers study how retrieved experience should be stored, timed, and inserted into world-action models, proposing the F3 method to make experience useful rather than harmful.
s60fb031f69.why: It suggests that reusing an agent's past rollouts can hurt performance unless storage, timing, and placement are designed carefully.

sba8aa04a9c.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
sba8aa04a9c.description: arXiv:2611.24845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes. Financial trading makes this limitation especially consequential: prices, news, market conditions, portfolio positions, and available capital evolve continuously. A result is useful only when it remains tied to the correct time, data snapshot, and execution context. We present Vibe-Trading, a comprehensive agent-native trading framework and all-in-one workspace for building, evaluating, and evolving agents for financial trading. It unifies market research, financial data, strategy generation, backtesting, portfolio ana
sba8aa04a9c.summary: Vibe-Trading is presented as an agent-native trading system designed to keep reliable state as prices, news, and portfolio conditions change.
sba8aa04a9c.why: It highlights the engineering challenge of keeping agent results tied to correct time, data snapshot, and execution context.

sb0eb9157f6.title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents
sb0eb9157f6.description: arXiv:2611.24867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual agents that read dense documents must ration a finite observation budget across candidate regions, yet answer accuracy conflates where an agent looks, how it adapts to the reads that remain, and how it an?swers once observation stops. We introduce budget-paired counterfactual audits, an evaluation protocol that holds public evidence and region bindings fixed while perturbing only the remaining budget or de?clared task parameters, and credits every acquired history with exact continuation values. The resulting accounting decomposes lost expected accuracy into stepwise acquisition loss and terminal decision loss, separating planning from fixed-role heuristics. Across forty paired routing anchors, five open-weight
sb0eb9157f6.summary: Researchers propose budget-paired counterfactual audits to evaluate visual document agents by separating where they look from how they answer.
sb0eb9157f6.why: It offers an evaluation method that separates observation strategy from answer quality, which matters for credible agent benchmarking.

saa4e3911d0.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
saa4e3911d0.description: arXiv:2611.24869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rules govern how player actions change interactive worlds. Different rules create distinct gameplay experiences within similar scenes and action spaces. For customizable gameplay, generative world models must follow user-defined rules beyond real-world behaviors. However, realizing user-defined rules presents two challenges: Rule-State Persistence and Rule-to-Visual Realization. The former requires preserving rule definitions, dependencies, and world states across saving and loading, so that restored worlds follow the established rules. The latter requires accurately realizing rule-induced changes on designated objects and attributes, particularly when affected objects are unseen. In this paper, we propose WorldRuler, which organizes rule def
saa4e3911d0.summary: WorldRuler is introduced as an interactive world-modeling approach that aims to make generative worlds follow user-defined rules across save and load.
saa4e3911d0.why: Keeping rule definitions and world state persistent is a concrete requirement for customizable generative game environments.

s20a8ac8a1d.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
s20a8ac8a1d.description: arXiv:2611.24880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in power electronics, where it drives the simulation loop that engineers used to close largely by hand. In this loop, a converter design, or a study of the network it connects to, is built, run, measured and revised until it satisfies its specification. Such an agent can be served from a cloud API or from an inference device on the premises. For organizations whose designs, customer data or export-controlled material cannot leave the site, and whose simulators are licensed there, local deployment is the natural choice. In such a deployment, the agent becomes an electrical load on the organization's own equipment, i.e., every run consumes power and energy on a local device, generates tokens and
s20a8ac8a1d.summary: A paper examines deploying local AI agents for power electronics simulation, covering deployment, measurements, and costs versus cloud APIs.
s20a8ac8a1d.why: Organizations with confidential designs or export-controlled material may need on-premises agent deployment, and this paper reports on its practical costs.

s04702621aa.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
s04702621aa.description: arXiv:2611.24932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value? We argue this is a question about a single cognitive trait, metacognitive calibration: the alignment between a reviewer's behavioral confidence and the actual correctness of their judgments. We develop a trait theory of reviewer value to make it precise. The theory makes five claims: value is governed by calibration rather than by activity, speed, agreement, or tenure; calibration leaves observable traces in behavioral telemetry; those traces are non-diagnostic on their own, because the fast, low-revision signature of a calibrated expert is indistinguishable from that of a confident novice until it is gated by outcomes; human calibration an
s04702621aa.summary: A paper proposes a trait theory holding that a human reviewer's value alongside AI depends on metacognitive calibration rather than activity, speed, or tenure.
s04702621aa.why: It offers a framework for deciding which human reviewers still add value in human-AI decision workflows.

sa1239befcd.title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
sa1239befcd.description: arXiv:2611.23244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. Recently, Dmitry Rybin announced a seven-vertex counterexample found through an interaction with ChatGPT, which disproved this long-standing conjecture. However, the interaction did not reveal why this particular topology and its demand, fractional-flow, and cost choices work together, whether the example belongs to a broader family, or which structural features determine where counterexamples can occur. It also left unclear why the AI-assisted search succeeded where earlier human efforts had not. In this paper, we develop a forward counterexamp
sa1239befcd.summary: A paper analyzes how an AI-assisted interaction with ChatGPT produced a seven-vertex counterexample to Goemans's unsplittable-flow conjecture, exploring its structure and family.
sa1239befcd.why: It examines how AI tools can contribute to mathematical counterexample discovery, though its direct relevance to engineering practice is limited.

s94197ae4e5.title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence
s94197ae4e5.description: arXiv:2611.23245v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Response-relevant information is not sufficient evidence that two neural networks are in the same training state. We define training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent, relative to an intervention family and horizon, if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continues. On fresh runs of a one-layer transformer learning modular addition, response to a weight-decay pulse is highly reproducible relative to between-checkpoint differences (rho_state = 0.934 at 500 steps), establishing the target as measurable. Fifteen descriptors of weight spectra, representation geometry and optimiser geometry carry within-run response-relevant information beyond weight norm and loss on a development dataset, predicting he
s94197ae4e5.summary: The paper argues that response-relevant information is not sufficient to show two neural networks are in the same training state, defining equivalence through perturbation responses.
s94197ae4e5.why: It cautions that matching outputs or task-relevant behavior does not prove two checkpoints are equivalent in training state.

s9bfed27f55.title: The Obsolescence of High-Level Code: Agentic Generation from Semantic Artifacts
s9bfed27f55.description: arXiv:2611.23249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper argues that high-level source code need not remain the primary persistent artifact of software development when AI agents can generate, validate, and regenerate executable implementations from semantic intent. We place this claim in historical context by revisiting application generators, CASE tools, model-driven development, and platforms such as GeneXus, where developers already maintained higher-level representations from which code and other artifacts were derived. We propose a unifying view in which generation is the fundamental operation: given a semantic specification S = (R, C, I, T, O), maintained as the semantic authority, an agent produces a generated executable artifact A. Functional requirements, contracts, and inter
s9bfed27f55.summary: The paper argues high-level source code may stop being the primary persistent artifact, as AI agents can regenerate executable implementations from semantic intent.
s9bfed27f55.why: It raises questions about whether engineering teams should maintain specifications rather than code as the durable artifact.

sc70c56d80c.title: What Moves the Ceiling on Automated Audit: from General Code to Scientific Code, Results and Data
sc70c56d80c.description: arXiv:2611.23250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Models increasingly check what other models write. We study one shipped arrangement, in which an auditor from a different vendor reads the work and deterministic checks verify what code can verify, and measure its limits against ground truth no model supplies. On general-purpose code with hidden tests, eight readings of the auditor reach 30.0% recall [20.0, 40.7] at 16.0% [10.1, 22.3] flags on correct code, with diminishing returns and no plateau. The reading model (confounded with its sampling), one rulebook sentence and the decision rule each move that figure, and much of what is missed is, on a post hoc rating, behaviour the specification never determined. In three preregistered science studies, checking that reported numbers trace to th
sc70c56d80c.summary: A study measures an automated auditor from a different vendor checking model-written code, reporting 30.0% recall at 16.0% flags on correct code on general-purpose tasks.
sc70c56d80c.why: It quantifies the limits of model-based code auditing, which matters for teams relying on AI reviewers for quality checks.

s8c1222fe8c.title: From Data Quality to Data Trustworthiness in AI-Driven Software-Intensive Embedded Systems: A Systematic Review
s8c1222fe8c.description: arXiv:2611.23252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-driven software-intensive embedded systems (SIES) depend on data during development and operation. Poor data quality (DQ) may weaken data trustworthiness, yet evidence about its effects and lifecycle management remains fragmented. This systematic literature review synthesizes 27 primary studies published from January 2020 to February 2026. It examines DQ concerns and evidence linking them to reduced data trustworthiness, along with assessment and management methods. The review identifies 16 concerns organized as Source Quality and Content Quality. Studies provide DQ-based scores and evidence of effects on model or decision performance. Synthesis suggests upstream source or handling problems may become embedded in training baselines and r
s8c1222fe8c.summary: A systematic review of 27 studies identifies 16 data quality concerns in AI-driven embedded systems and how they affect data trustworthiness.
s8c1222fe8c.why: It organizes known data quality risks and assessment methods relevant to teams building AI into embedded products.

s20ed88de57.title: Measuring What Matters in the Age of AI: The Research Software Metrics Landscape
s20ed88de57.description: arXiv:2611.23253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Research software now serves as a primary instrument of science, but the methods the community uses to judge its quality, sustainability, reuse, and impact remain scattered across software engineering, open science, FAIR software, citation, and research-assessment literature. AI-assisted development sharpens the problem: code can be produced at rates that outpace human review capacity, provenance and attribution are harder to track, scholarly credit systems cannot keep pace, and existing metrics inherit assumptions about how research software gets developed that may no longer apply. To aid in navigating these challenges, we present a focused landscape synthesis of research software metrics based on 49 substantive references, organizing the
s20ed88de57.summary: A paper surveys research software metrics for quality, sustainability, reuse, and impact, arguing AI-assisted development strains existing measures.
s20ed88de57.why: AI-generated code outpacing review capacity challenges how research software quality and provenance are judged.

sd57893509b.title: Generative AI in Software Testing: Practitioners' Perspectives on the Benefits, Challenges, Opportunities, and Risks
sd57893509b.description: arXiv:2611.23256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) increasingly supports software testing, yet empirical evidence on practitioners' perceptions remains limited. This study investigates perceived benefits, challenges, opportunities, and risks of GenAI in software testing through a questionnaire survey of 64 practitioners. Closed-ended responses were analyzed descriptively, while open-ended responses were qualitatively coded to contextualize the findings. Among the respondents, 34 were users (those with regular or experimental use of GenAI in testing) and 30 were non-users (those without prior use of GenAI in testing). Results show generally positive perceptions of GenAI for reducing effort, test generation, and debugging, alongside concerns about pr
sd57893509b.summary: A questionnaire survey of 64 practitioners examines perceived benefits, challenges, and risks of generative AI in software testing.
sd57893509b.why: It provides practitioner-reported evidence on where GenAI helps and where it creates risk in testing workflows.

s8418a89b37.title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
s8418a89b37.description: arXiv:2611.23257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines do not expose. We introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes a checkpoint, an artifact that restores that state and can be versioned and replayed, from a natural-language functional test case and read-only access to the target's source code. The checkpoint is restored through a per-application hook that an onboarding agent binds or synthesizes
s8418a89b37.summary: Researchers introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes versionable, replayable checkpoints to restore deep states in self-rendered GUI software for testing.
s8418a89b37.why: Reusable checkpoints could cut the recurring cost of reaching deep states in GUI tests across commits, where DOM-based automation is unavailable.

s0b033cc335.title: EnvAgent: Multi-Agent Approach to Building Science Environments in the Clouds
s0b033cc335.description: arXiv:2611.23258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents are transforming scientific computing and software workflows, but generating and executing code requires a correctly configured execution environment. Automating environment construction remains difficult because repositories encode heterogeneous, often incomplete requirements for operating systems, toolchains, dependencies, and build procedures. Existing workflows thus rely on developer-maintained Dockerfiles and setup scripts, making preparation labor-intensive, hard to scale, and potentially biasing evaluations. We present ENVAGENT, an agentic framework that synthesizes, builds, and verifies repository-level Docker environments. ENVAGENT combines deterministic utilities for Docker execution and state management with coordinated
s0b033cc335.summary: Researchers present EnvAgent, a multi-agent system that automates building execution environments for repositories, replacing hand-maintained Dockerfiles and setup scripts.
s0b033cc335.why: Automating environment setup could reduce labor-intensive preparation and make running scientific and software code easier to scale.

s8e5aa7c122.title: Ephyra: A Property-Based Testing Framework for the LLM Era
s8e5aa7c122.description: arXiv:2611.23282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents now write a growing share of software tests; however, property-based testing (PBT) libraries are designed with historical considerations. We present Ephyra, a PBT library in Rust built on three concepts: customizability, observability and generator synthesis. Ephyra lets users compose their own testing loops from generation, mutation and shrinking, and synthesize these components to satisfy functional predicates. Applying Ephyra to 14 open source systems, we have found 349 bugs and reported 300 of them, in database management systems (SQLite, Turso, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, DataFusion), the verified policy engine (Cedar), the SQL equivalence prover (QED), the URL parser used in Node.js (ada-url), reimplementations of existing open
s8e5aa7c122.summary: Ephyra, a Rust property-based testing library designed for LLM-era coding agents, reportedly found 349 bugs across 14 open source systems, with 300 reported.
s8e5aa7c122.why: Tools built for agent-written tests may surface more defects in widely used open source databases and systems.

scb70bcba15.title: When Single Agent Is Enough: Rethinking Multi-Agent Systems for Automated Code Review
scb70bcba15.description: arXiv:2611.23283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Code review plays a critical role in identifying software quality issues and ensuring system robustness. Prior work has proposed techniques for Review Comment Generation (RCG) and Code Refinement (CR), with recent Multi-Agent (MA) approaches achieving state-of-the-art results by coordinating agents specialized in different quality dimensions. However, MA systems introduce substantial architectural complexity and runtime overhead, and recent evidence suggests they may underperform Single-Agent (SA) approaches in certain tasks. In this work, we systematically compare MA and SA designs for RCG and CR. Surprisingly, our results show that SA approaches perform comparably to- and sometimes outperform-MA systems, despite their simpler design. Thes
scb70bcba15.summary: A study questions whether multi-agent systems are needed for automated code review, comparing them against single-agent approaches on review comment generation and refinement.
scb70bcba15.why: Single-agent designs may match multi-agent results with less architectural complexity and runtime overhead, informing code review tool choices.

s22d268c78b.title: The Illusion of Relief: How GenAI Redistributes Cognitive Workload in Software Organizations
s22d268c78b.description: arXiv:2611.23286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study explores how Generative AI (GenAI) reshapes software practitioners' cognitive work across software development activities. We analyzed questionnaire responses from 44 practitioners across nine organizations using descriptive quantitative methods and qualitative analysis of relevant open-ended responses. Practitioners reported productivity and time savings, but also effort associated with providing context, prompting, reviewing, correcting, verifying, and integrating AI-generated outputs. Human judgment and accountability remained central, with practitioners anticipating a shift from direct code production to guiding, evaluating, validating, integrating, and coordinating AI-supported work. Thus, GenAI appears to redistribute cogni
s22d268c78b.summary: A survey of 44 practitioners across nine organizations finds GenAI saves time but adds cognitive effort in providing context, prompting, reviewing, and verifying outputs.
s22d268c78b.why: Time savings from AI coding tools may be partly offset by verification and integration work, which leaders should account for when measuring productivity.

s7049294cb6.title: Ask the Peers: Ranking NFR Coverage Gaps for Requirements Review
s7049294cb6.description: arXiv:2611.23296v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Missing or underrepresented non-functional requirements (NFR) categories leave little direct evidence in a requirements set, making them difficult to identify during requirements review. In this study, we frame NFR coverage-gap review as a project-level ranking task: given a target requirements specification, the goal is to rank the 11 PROMISE NFR categories for analyst inspection. We compare seven statistical, embedding-based, and large language model (LLM)-based configurations that differ in both ranking mechanism and evidence source, including target requirement statements, peer requirements, their semantic representation, and peer category statistics. We evaluate the configurations using controlled gap injection with leave-one-project-o
s7049294cb6.summary: Researchers compare seven statistical, embedding, and LLM-based methods for ranking missing non-functional requirement categories during requirements review.
s7049294cb6.why: Ranking coverage gaps could help analysts spot underspecified quality requirements earlier in requirements review.

s5d31244728.title: When Code Works but the License Doesn't: Evaluating License Constraint Handling in Coding Agents
s5d31244728.description: arXiv:2611.23299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly undertake repository-level development, including dependency selection, source modification, and software deployment. However, existing evaluations prioritize functional success over licensing correctness and commercial suitability. We investigate whether agents recognize and preserve software-license constraints when developing proprietary software. Experiments across multiple agents examine permissive and copyleft licenses, missing licensing information, transitive dependencies, source modification, dual licensing, vendoring, and distribution contexts. Agent traces, repository changes, and final artifacts are evaluated against licensing ground truth. Results reveal a persistent gap between functional and licensi
s5d31244728.summary: A study finds coding agents often fail to recognize or preserve software license constraints, since evaluations prioritize functional success over licensing correctness.
s5d31244728.why: Teams using coding agents on proprietary code may face unnoticed license violations, so licensing checks belong in agent evaluation and review.

s46115d46b8.title: Dependency Fabrication in Repository Deployment Agents
s46115d46b8.description: arXiv:2611.23305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Repository deployment agents set up the environment needed to run a software repository. They often treat passing tests as proof of a successful setup. This report examines how such agents behave when a working setup is impossible. Probe repositories were built with a dependency that the agents could not legitimately obtain. Passing tests therefore indicated fabrication, such as creating a stub to replace the missing package. Agents in Repo2Run and SetupX usually fabricated the dependency. Both harnesses mostly still marked these runs as successful. Rules against fabrication, whether given in the prompt or repository documentation, did not reliably prevent this behavior. On MinimalSetupAgent, which was built for this report, mitigations pro
s46115d46b8.summary: A report finds repository deployment agents often fabricate missing dependencies, such as stubs, and harnesses still mark these runs as successful when tests pass.
s46115d46b8.why: Passing tests can hide fabricated setups, so teams relying on agent-driven deployment need independent verification of environment success.

s968b5367df.title: Repository-Grounded Rubrics for Execution-Free Evaluation of Coding Agents
s968b5367df.description: arXiv:2611.23309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents are usually evaluated by running task-specific tests, but tests may be missing or incomplete, and running them requires a working environment for each repository. We adapt agentic rubrics, introduced for selecting among candidate patches, into an execution-free measure of how far a patch satisfies a task's requirements. An agent explores the repository before the change and writes weighted binary criteria, and a judge without tools scores a diff by the weighted share of criteria it satisfies. We validate the ordering this score produces against test outcomes on SWE-bench Verified, using 7,291 labeled patches from fifteen systems. Within the 400 tasks that have both resolved and unresolved patches, the mean per-task AUROC is 0.
s968b5367df.summary: Researchers propose execution-free evaluation of coding agents using weighted rubric criteria written by an agent and scored by a tool-less judge on diffs.
s968b5367df.why: Rubric-based scoring without running tests could evaluate patches in repositories where tests are missing or environments are hard to set up.

s5b84507c6d.title: Reusing formal Vlasov-Maxwell proofs to certify plasma solver outputs
s5b84507c6d.description: arXiv:2611.23319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI now produces machine-checked mathematics faster than researchers can read it. Can such theorems do practical computational work? We reuse one from \mbox{OpenAI's} Lean~4 relativistic Vlasov--Maxwell library: initial fields determine the field at an outside point until plasma signals reach it, and the energy leaving a surrounding box before they reach its faces. New Lean proofs and numerical bounds give particle-free references for particle-in-cell simulations across three tasks. Domain size follows analytically from observation time, exposing boundary and initialization errors in WarpX and Smilei that global energy checks missed. Grid choice can be tested directly: combining two coarse grids recovers unknown plasma inputs within toleranc
s5b84507c6d.summary: Researchers reuse a formal Lean 4 Vlasov-Maxwell library from OpenAI to produce machine-checked particle-free reference bounds for checking plasma simulation outputs.
s5b84507c6d.why: Formally verified theorems can provide checkable references for numerical simulation outputs, an approach relevant to certifying scientific computing.

saf41eea05a.title: HydroMind: A Checkable Agent for Autonomous Hydrological Research
saf41eea05a.description: arXiv:2611.23323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General-purpose coding agents have written code for hydrological and Earth-system models. In these studies the researchers decided in advance how the model would be evaluated, for example the test period, the scoring function, and the standard the model had to meet. No study has tested what happens when the agent makes these decisions itself: how many of its claims are supported by its own data, code, and results, and whether readers can check them. Both may depend on the agent's harness, that is, the tools it can call and the written instructions it follows. We compared three harnesses: the agent's own harness; this harness plus the modeling tools of HydroMind, a hydrological modeling system we developed for general-purpose agents, which r
saf41eea05a.summary: HydroMind is presented as a checkable agent for autonomous hydrological research, studying whether an agent's own claims are supported by its data, code, and results.
saf41eea05a.why: Agents making their own evaluation decisions raise verifiability questions that matter for any autonomous research or analysis workflow.

s49a89cf420.title: Optimize the Cob, Then the Kernel: Optimizing Beam Search for Generative Recommendation Inference
s49a89cf420.description: arXiv:2611.23339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. Existing LLM serving engines such as vLLM process beams as batched independent sequences, causing redundant KV cache accesses over the shared prompt prefix. Furthermore, vLLM executes each beam search generation step as a separate engine invocation, incurring host-side beam processing overhead between decoding steps and substantial runtime KV block management in PagedAttention. Using Tree Attention, we concatenate beams along the sequence dimension to eliminate redundant KV accesses, and further optimize execution through pre-generated partial-attention masks, sta
s49a89cf420.summary: Researchers propose optimizations to beam search for generative recommendation inference, reducing redundant KV cache access that vLLM incurs on shared prompt prefixes.
s49a89cf420.why: Inference engines for generative recommenders may need specialized beam search and KV cache handling to cut serving cost and latency.

sf0c5ab617a.title: Management of Behavioral Addictions via Artificial Intelligence based Digital Technologies
sf0c5ab617a.description: arXiv:2611.23341v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Behavioral addictions, such as problematic gaming, gambling, social media use, and online shopping, have emerged as a growing global concern with significant psychological, social, and economic consequences. Traditional assessment and treatment approaches, while clinically grounded, often struggle with scalability, accessibility, and long-term engagement. In recent years, advances in digital technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled the development of novel, data-driven solutions for the prevention, detection, treatment, and recovery of behavioral addictions. This book presents a comprehensive survey of the management of behavioral addictions through digital technologies, bridging clinical foundations with state-of-the-art
sf0c5ab617a.summary: A review examines how AI-based digital technologies could help prevent, detect, and treat behavioral addictions such as gaming, gambling, and social media overuse.
sf0c5ab617a.why: The text gives too little technical detail to say much for engineers or tech leaders.

s709be627c8.title: Confidence-Based Materials Data Quality Assessment via Domain Knowledge and Graph-Structured Learning
s709be627c8.description: arXiv:2611.23342v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid development of materials machine learning relies on large-scale, heterogeneous datasets, yet model reliability is often compromised by imperfect data from diverse experiments, simulations, and database integration. Real-world materials databases may contain measurement errors, failed calculations, missing or duplicate records, and hidden violations of physicochemical constraints. Such problems are difficult to identify because corrupted samples may remain statistically plausible rather than appearing as explicit outliers. In this paper, we propose a confidence-based materials data quality assessment framework that integrates domain knowledge with graph-structured learning. Data quality is formulated as a continuous confidence esti
s709be627c8.summary: Researchers propose a confidence-based method combining domain knowledge and graph-structured learning to assess data quality in materials databases.
s709be627c8.why: Detecting plausible but corrupted records could improve reliability of machine learning trained on heterogeneous materials data.

sefdc94a2dc.title: BiMa-ECGSR: reconstructing the 12-lead ECG from reduced lead sets with bidirectional state-space models
sefdc94a2dc.description: arXiv:2611.23345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wearables and monitors record few electrocardiogram (ECG) leads; most diagnostic tools assume 12 leads. BiMa-ECGSR reconstructs the 12-lead ECG from reduced lead sets with a bidirectional Mamba state-space encoder--decoder, as regression (BiMa-SR) or diffusion (DiBiMa-SR). Models were trained on PTB-XL for six input sets (I; II; I+II; I+II+V1; I+II+V2; I+II+V1+V4), see only the measured leads at inference, and were tested on the PTB-XL test fold (2,198 records) and two external cohorts (Georgia, 10,275 records; Chapman-Shaoxing/Ningbo, 43,559). From lead II alone, the pooled median Pearson correlation (PCC) over the 11 predicted leads was 0.914 on PTB-XL, against 0.784 for a least-squares linear filter (lead I: 0.906 against 0.789). As limb
sefdc94a2dc.summary: BiMa-ECGSR uses bidirectional Mamba state-space models to reconstruct 12-lead ECGs from reduced lead sets, via regression or diffusion, tested on PTB-XL and external cohorts.
sefdc94a2dc.why: Reconstructing full 12-lead ECGs from few leads could let wearables and monitors feed tools that assume standard 12-lead input.

s1e6751808c.title: SurgCBVR: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Content-Based Surgical Video-to-Video Retrieval
s1e6751808c.description: arXiv:2611.23347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hospitals record thousands of hours of surgical video annually, yet these archives remain difficult to search by content. Surgeons cannot readily retrieve similar operations, complications, or workflow events. Existing surgical computer vision primarily produces labels rather than retrieving relevant videos. We introduce SurgCBVR, the first benchmark for content-based video-to-video retrieval in surgery. It integrates eight public datasets across four domains-ophthalmic, laparoscopic, robotic-assisted, and colonoscopy-covering six procedure types, 679 cases, and 76,489 clips (106 hours). SurgCBVR comprises two tiers: Scene, retrieving the same operative state across cases and sites, and Workflow, retrieving and localizing phase transitions
s1e6751808c.summary: Researchers introduced SurgCBVR, a benchmark for content-based video-to-video retrieval of surgical videos, integrating eight public datasets across four surgical domains.
s1e6751808c.why: Gives teams a standard way to evaluate retrieval of similar surgical videos, moving beyond label-only surgical vision systems.

scb0fb7ebb8.title: SIGMA: speaker-isolated, symptom-structured multimodal estimation of depression severity from clinical interviews
scb0fb7ebb8.description: arXiv:2611.23348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical interviews are central to depression assessment but time-consuming and rater-dependent. Automated severity estimation offers scalable screening, yet existing methods often retain interviewer speech (confounding participant cues), fuse modalities late (losing fine-grained cross-modal dynamics), or score symptoms independently (ignoring inter-symptom correlations). We present SIGMA, a speaker-aware, symptom-structured framework for depression-severity estimation from semi-clinical interviews. SIGMA uses speaker diarization to restrict input to participant speech, cross-attention so that text, audio and video condition one another during encoding, and a graded-response head that predicts the eight questionnaire items jointly through a
scb0fb7ebb8.summary: Researchers propose SIGMA, a multimodal framework that estimates depression severity from clinical interviews by isolating speaker audio and modeling symptoms jointly.
scb0fb7ebb8.why: Shows architectural choices like speaker diarization and early cross-modal fusion that may matter for multimodal health-screening systems.

s72550b2635.title: Systematic Mapping Protocol. Generative AI-Augmented Requirements Engineering: A Systematic Mapping Study of Practices, Specifications, and Reuse in Software Development
s72550b2635.description: arXiv:2611.23349v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models (LLMs), is rapidly being adopted in requirements engineering (RE). Existing secondary studies have characterized which RE activities are supported and which prompting strategies are used, but little is known about the specifications that GenAI-augmented RE produces and how they are used in subsequent activities such as specification-driven development (SDD), design and code generation, test derivation, verification, and reuse. This document presents the protocol of a systematic mapping study (SMS) that will identify and classify research on GenAI-augmented RE, with particular attention to the work products it generates and their downstream use. The protocol defin
s72550b2635.summary: Authors published a protocol for a systematic mapping study on how generative AI is used in requirements engineering, including specifications and reuse.

scc609398a1.title: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions
scc609398a1.description: arXiv:2611.23353v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a language-model agent's tool call is interrupted, the action may already have changed an external system without confirmation. Retrying risks duplication; assuming success may conceal an action that never occurred. We study these failure modes in a controlled agent runtime combining authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing. We inject ten single-host fault classes and compare four configurations and three ablations using a target-side oracle separate from the runtime ledger. On each of Windows and Linux, 7,513 trials used 96 captured model responses from 24 constructed cases. In 200 known original crash and replay pairs, the full configuration recorded 0/200 repeated effects versus
scc609398a1.summary: Researchers ran a fault-injection study of language-model agent tool actions, comparing configurations that handle interrupted calls via idempotency, ledgers, and reconciliation.
scc609398a1.why: Highlights that retries and idempotency alone do not guarantee recovery when agent tool calls fail mid-action on external systems.

s86d54a6df6.title: Implementing Binary Transformers with Approximate Memories with Permutation Invariance Enabled Selective (PIES) Protection
s86d54a6df6.description: arXiv:2611.23358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantization is an effective technique to reduce memory storage, computation complexity and power for Transformers, and the binarization of the weights is important for meeting these requirements. Approximate memory can further reduce the power for memory, but it also introduces errors. Current research for binary Transformers focuses on task performance, but the model dependable operation against errors on the memory has not been well studied. In this paper, we first evaluate the dependability of binary Transformers with the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) as a case study. A large accuracy loss occurs only at high Bit Error Rates (e.g. BER = 5% or 10%). Then we propose a novel Permutation Invariance Enabled S
s86d54a6df6.summary: Researchers evaluate the dependability of binary Transformers stored in approximate memory and propose Permutation Invariance Enabled Selective (PIES) protection against memory errors.
s86d54a6df6.why: Relevant to engineers deploying quantized models on low-power hardware where memory bit errors can degrade model reliability.

scecba1c55c.title: Image Watermarking With Memory Across Reissuance
scecba1c55c.description: arXiv:2611.23363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Publishers often revise and reissue images, yet valid watermarks may persist on superseded releases or unapproved edits. Even a current release can contain regions last authorized at different revisions. We introduce and formalize reissuable provenance: determining an image's current, superseded, or unissued status and recovering each region's last authorized revision (its generation), with abstention when evidence is insufficient. Generational Stratigraphy Fields (GSF) combine watermark evidence with an authenticated live reference to the current release, enabling replacement or retirement without rewriting circulated copies. Each reissue freshly embeds new generation labels in approved regions and inherited labels elsewhere, preserving hi
scecba1c55c.summary: Researchers introduce Generational Stratigraphy Fields, a watermarking method that determines whether an image is current, superseded, or unissued and recovers each region's last authorized revision.
scecba1c55c.why: Offers a provenance approach for publishers who reissue images, useful for content authenticity pipelines.

sa11781c306.title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion
sa11781c306.description: arXiv:2611.23364v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Animals generate behavior through continuous interactions between their neural circuits, bodies, and environment. Embodied simulations study these interactions by testing neural circuit models in biologically realistic settings. Recent efforts have simulated diverse animals, and emerging work on biologically grounded neural architectures has begun to integrate circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics from experimental data into artificial neural networks, introducing stronger inductive biases and closer mechanistic alignment with biology. How can we develop embodied simulations that enable the study of increasingly complex bodies and neural circuits? In this work, we address the challenge through coordinated advances in the simulated b
sa11781c306.summary: Researchers present neural circuit architectural priors for simulating rat locomotion, integrating circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics into artificial neural networks.

s5541d6f2d8.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
s5541d6f2d8.description: arXiv:2611.23388v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. As a result, experts must redesign it for every new model, which is time-consuming and often sub-optimal. Fortunately, an LLM agent can take over this design by refining the recipe over rounds of building and evaluating candidates, so that more rounds lead to better recipes. However, evaluating one quantized reasoning model takes tens of GPU-hours, and combining methods from different codebases means porting each to the new architecture by hand. We present QDA, a system in which an agent designs the recipe for each model and precision. To make evaluation fast, QDA scores each
s5541d6f2d8.summary: Researchers present QDA, a closed-loop system where an LLM agent designs post-training quantization recipes by iteratively building and evaluating candidates.
s5541d6f2d8.why: Suggests agents can automate model quantization tuning, a costly per-model task, though evaluation takes tens of GPU-hours per reasoning model.

sa951d73646.title: Which Tokens, in What Order, and How Fast? A Theoretical Analysis of On-Policy Distillation Objectives
sa951d73646.description: arXiv:2611.23397v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student language model to match a teacher model based on its own generations. When using OPD, one must choose whether to apply it at the sequence or token level and which divergence to minimize. However, despite the wide adoption of OPD in practice, the formal understanding of which OPD objective is appropriate for a given setting is limited. Toward addressing this gap, we theoretically analyze how the choice of OPD objective governs which tokens are prioritized, in what order, and how efficiently. Our analysis reveals that sequence-level OPD exhibits a future agreement bias, which myopic token-level objectives avoid. This bias induces a reverse learning order, in which sequence-level OPD first matches
sa951d73646.summary: A theoretical analysis examines how sequence-level versus token-level on-policy distillation objectives prioritize tokens, their order, and their efficiency when training student language models.
sa951d73646.why: Helps practitioners choose between sequence- and token-level distillation objectives and divergences for training smaller language models.

s438f6cf940.title: Tracking Representations in LLM Reasoning Traces for Iterated Games
s438f6cf940.description: arXiv:2611.23403v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents achieve state-of-the-art performance across domains through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning. Despite their ubiquitous use, little is understood about the relationship between the externalized trace and the model's actual computation. We address this by investigating how LLM agents make decisions in iterative games with incomplete information. Using a series of mechanistic interpretability techniques, we find that the model forms and iteratively revises an internal representation of the game throughout the CoT. Once the model prematurely commits to an incorrect belief, it rarely recovers. This failure is manifested in both the literal trace and the layer activations. Ultimately, as multi-agent systems are m
s438f6cf940.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability, researchers find LLM agents form and revise an internal game representation throughout their chain-of-thought in iterated games with incomplete information.
s438f6cf940.why: Suggests chain-of-thought traces may not fully reflect the model's internal computation, relevant for debugging and trusting agent reasoning.

s72167d8756.title: Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones
s72167d8756.description: arXiv:2611.23446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Compact convolutional backbones such as EfficientNet achieve strong parameter efficiency through local depthwise separable convolutions, yet two structural questions remain central to hybrid design: where does global self-attention improve recognition over pure convolution, and can repeated blocks share weights without losing representational capacity? We investigate both questions on ImageNet-1k (50,000-image validation) using controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments. First, we show that wrapping a classification backbone in multi-scale feature pyramids (BiFPN) fails to outperform a plain MBConv trunk (69.99% - 71.81% vs. 72.86% plain B0) until paired with stage attention (73.15%). In contrast, keeping the MBConv trunk intact and inserting l
s72167d8756.summary: Controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments on ImageNet-1k examine where global self-attention helps compact vision backbones and whether repeated blocks can share weights.
s72167d8756.why: Provides design guidance on placing attention and weight sharing in compact hybrid vision backbones for efficiency-constrained deployments.

s13ce96e8e7.title: Reliability by Architecture: Agentic Workflows for Validated Multi-Physics Simulation from Natural Language
s13ce96e8e7.description: arXiv:2611.23473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preparing, executing, and validating strongly coupled multi-physics simulations require expert time. Agentic workflows use large language models (LLMs) to coordinate them from natural-language descriptions, but reliability requires checks of physical consistency and fidelity to the problem description. Our agentic harness implements explicit task allocation: LLMs interpret user requests and simulator diagnostics, generate input components not covered by predefined construction rules, and propose repairs, while deterministic routines construct supported components and check inputs, edits, and results. We evaluate CO2-storage problems using the multi-physics simulator GEOS, from compositional flow to flow-poromechanics with frictional fault c
s13ce96e8e7.summary: Researchers present an agentic harness where LLMs handle request interpretation and repairs while deterministic routines build validated multi-physics simulations from natural language.
s13ce96e8e7.why: Demonstrates splitting work between LLMs and deterministic code to make agent-driven engineering simulation pipelines more reliable.

s6e5ac5a0a6.title: AllotNet: an Interpretable Mixture-of-Experts Choice Model for Moral Judgement in Humanitarian Aid Allocation, Validated against a Planted Synthetic Population
s6e5ac5a0a6.description: arXiv:2611.23474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Official development assistance fell by 23.1 per cent in 2025, and the decision of who is helped first when there is not enough for everyone is moving into software. A leading published machine-learning targeting system excluded 53 per cent of eligible households as deployed. If the rule of distribution ends up in code, it should carry the judgement of many cultures, and the machine should execute while a person judges. AllotNet is an interpretable mixture-of-experts conditional logit for the allocation judgements elicited by Allot, a pre-registered six-language instrument: eight linear taste experts over seven ethical criteria, weighted by a gate over participant context, with a damped residual, an encoder for household intake, an outcome
s6e5ac5a0a6.summary: Researchers introduce AllotNet, an interpretable mixture-of-experts choice model for humanitarian aid allocation decisions, validated against a planted synthetic population.
s6e5ac5a0a6.why: Raises concerns about encoding moral judgments in allocation software, with interpretability offered as a way to audit such systems.

sde3699ea88.title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
sde3699ea88.description: arXiv:2611.23498v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulating how physical systems respond to changing conditions is central to control, design, and scenario studies. To our knowledge, prior PDE foundation models have not been trained or evaluated on changes within trajectories. Our counterfactual test measures how far predictions move toward a changed solver branch from the same state. Models trained on fixed conditions follow changes only partly. A PDE foundation model given a condition input after pretraining barely responds. PhysDial adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight two-dimensional PDE families. Coefficients enter with the noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equation text as a prompt. In Kolmogorov flow, switches within trajectories account for
sde3699ea88.summary: PhysDial adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer to simulate PDEs under changing physical conditions, addressing limited responsiveness of prior PDE foundation models.

seebbd674c9.title: Beyond the Sink Token: Sink-Guided Key Editing in Vision-Language Models
seebbd674c9.description: arXiv:2611.23516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In vision-language models (VLMs), a few sink tokens attract a disproportionate share of attention. While previous studies have examined why these tokens attract attention, we investigate how the sink-key direction affects attention to image and question tokens. Across four probed VLMs, boosting the magnitude of positive sink-aligned components increases attention on average, whereas boosting negative components decreases it; these responses persist through later layers. This identifies the native sink key as a reference for controlling attention beyond its own position. Motivated by this finding, we propose SHRINK, a training-free method that partially reduces sink-aligned components across visible keys during generation. On nine benchmarks
seebbd674c9.summary: Researchers show that boosting sink-aligned key components in vision-language models shifts attention toward image and question tokens, using the sink key as a control reference.
seebbd674c9.why: Offers a lightweight editing technique for steering attention in VLMs without retraining, relevant to interpretability and inference control.

s520ef181f8.title: Language Models Make New Research Sound Old
s520ef181f8.description: arXiv:2611.23546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Researchers are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) to validate research questions. We find that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate what related papers establish. Models recognize most of these overstatements when asked to check the papers' full texts separately. On 40 questions drawn from newly accepted papers, GPT-6-Astra correctly judges 98% to be unstudied, but states that status plainly in only 8% of ordinary answers. All six frontier systems show reporting gaps of 30-90 percentage points. Across 22 models given identical papers, higher capability is associated with more accurate judgments and larger reporting gaps. This reporting failure is asymmetric: models correctly identify studied que
s520ef181f8.summary: A preprint reports that LLMs make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate prior papers, though models flag most overstatements when checking full texts separately.
s520ef181f8.why: Engineers using LLMs for research validation should expect overstated novelty and verify claims against source papers rather than trusting plain answers.

s76ffef498f.title: Panini- Feasible Grammar For Robot Designs
s76ffef498f.description: arXiv:2611.23567v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symbolic methods make robot designs interpretable but often overlook continuous geometry; learned methods handle geometry but offer less transparent structure. We introduce a typed production grammar that uses case-role relations, parameter inheritance, and specificity-based rule arbitration to generate both manipulation skills and robot morphologies. A geometric realization map translates grammar composition into transformations in SE(3), behaving as a monoid homomorphism when inheritance is inactive and exhibiting a measurable defect when inheritance is enabled. The grammar provides a compact representation, and its arbitration decisions can be recovered from geometric containment (agreement 0.905 +/- 0.062 across 10 seeds, versus 0.611 +
s76ffef498f.summary: Researchers introduce a typed production grammar that generates robot manipulation skills and morphologies, mapping grammar composition to SE(3) transformations.

s1a8b51cf0d.title: ExiST: Existence-Aware Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Multi-Organ Segmentation
s1a8b51cf0d.description: arXiv:2611.23581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semi-supervised multi-organ segmentation should learn more than a dozen organs from a handful of labeled scans, and the smallest organs occupy less than one percent of the foreground. We identify a failure mode of self-training that is specific to this regime. When a teacher misses a small organ in a scan, every voxel of that organ receives the confident pseudo-label background, and the student is trained toward the organ absence. Repeated over many scans, this loop extinguishes tail organs. In a pilot study, removing the gallbladder from the pseudo-labels reduced its Dice on AMOS from 36.5 to 1.0. We argue that a missing organ should be treated as unresolved rather than absent and propose Existence-aware Self-Training (ExiST). It builds ps
s1a8b51cf0d.summary: Researchers propose ExiST, an existence-aware self-training method to stop semi-supervised models from erasing small organs in multi-organ segmentation.
s1a8b51cf0d.why: Teams training segmentation models with few labels may see small-class collapse from self-training loops, which this method targets.

sa152ff90d5.title: Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients for Stable Feature Attribution
sa152ff90d5.description: arXiv:2611.23600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Path-based attribution methods like Integrated Gradients (IG) are widely used to interpret neural networks, yet imperceptible input perturbations can drastically alter their attribution maps while leaving model predictions unchanged. We introduce Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients (ERIG), a path-based attribution method that intrinsically attenuates gradient irregularities along the integration path using maximum-entropy softmax weighting with temperature parameter $\tau$. We quantify the effect of the entropy-regularized weighting on attribution stability by using the Lipschitz properties of the model and its gradients. We decompose the attribution change under an input perturbation into a model-response term, whose bound is $\tau$-i
sa152ff90d5.summary: Researchers introduce Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients, an attribution method that reduces sensitivity of attribution maps to imperceptible input perturbations.
sa152ff90d5.why: Engineers relying on attribution maps for interpretability may get more stable explanations from this method, though the text gives limited evidence beyond the abstract.

seceea3853e.title: FutureBench: A Renewable Framework for Evaluating Knowledge-Context Conflict in LLMs
seceea3853e.description: arXiv:2611.23601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Asking a model to check retrieved text can also tell it which source to trust. We introduce FutureBench, a renewable framework for evaluating knowledge-context conflict using timestamped questions, controlled passage triplets, and no-context probes. Across 3,629 questions and six models, Verify (a prompt combining checking with passage priority) raises false-answer adoption in all five models tested on pre-cutoff events, mainly by displacing answers that were correct under Baseline, which allows both passage evidence and model knowledge. On post-cutoff events, only o4-mini increases adoption (+13.7 percentage points). A four-prompt comparison on 902 post-cutoff questions finds that passage priority without checking raises adoption, while mo
seceea3853e.summary: FutureBench, a renewable benchmark, tests how LLMs handle conflicts between retrieved passages and their own knowledge, finding a verification prompt increases false-answer adoption.
seceea3853e.why: A prompt asking models to check retrieved text can make them adopt wrong passage answers, a risk for RAG system designers to test.

s9cda9ddd15.title: JEPA as a Transferable Optimizer: Learning and Understanding Black-Box Optimization from Reward-Agnostic Pretraining
s9cda9ddd15.description: arXiv:2611.23608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Black-box optimization evaluates candidates through simulations, rollouts, or experiments, often without gradients. Learned optimizers are usually judged by whether they outperform existing methods. We ask a complementary question: what information does a learned optimizer use from its search history? We introduce JEPA-PS (JEPA Policy Search), based on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture. It is pretrained on random rollouts using parameter vectors and scalar returns. Its latent-prediction objective predicts the next point in an optimization trajectory rather than its reward or gradient, allowing us to examine what was tried and how well it performed. At test time, JEPA-PS reads a short evaluation history and proposes a candidate in on
s9cda9ddd15.summary: Researchers present JEPA-PS, a learned black-box optimizer pretrained on random rollouts, and study what information it uses from search history.

sb81e012136.title: MANGO Arena: Same Seeds, Different Chains Evaluating LLM Agents in a Disrupted Supply Chain
sb81e012136.description: arXiv:2611.23613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce MANGO Arena, an open-source testbed in which four LLM agents each run one company in a serial supply chain adapted from MANGO, a classroom factory-management game. The environment enforces hard rules (a truck limit, a no-credit cash constraint and production capacity), logs every blocked attempt to break them, and gives agents a public message board on which side payments are explicitly forbidden. This lets one environment measure three things at once: an economic outcome (the bullwhip effect), rule adherence under pressure, and proposals to collude. In a pilot with three small reasoning models, two scripted reference policies, two conditions (with and without a supplier fire) and three demand seeds, all LLM agents amplified de
sb81e012136.summary: Researchers released MANGO Arena, an open-source testbed where four LLM agents run companies in a disrupted supply chain, measuring economics, rule adherence, and cooperation.
sb81e012136.why: Useful for teams evaluating multi-agent LLM systems under hard constraints, since it measures rule compliance alongside economic outcomes.

s2ac2dd9dc8.title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair
s2ac2dd9dc8.description: arXiv:2611.23615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In weight-space programming, a language model edits a network's weights directly, without gradients. We ask what a successful repair of this kind relies on. We plant faults in the weights of two vision-language models, SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and check each edit made by a coding agent against the original weights. Without being told where to look, the agent finds rescaled rows in the projector and noise in the vision encoder of both models, infers the unknown scale factors, restores most or all of the rescaled weights to their exact original values, and returns accuracy to near its original level; programs that it writes from such weights repair unseen checkpoints of the same model without feedback. These repairs depend on a trace of
s2ac2dd9dc8.summary: Researchers show a coding agent can repair planted faults in vision-language model weights directly, without gradients, by inferring scale factors and restoring original values.
s2ac2dd9dc8.why: Suggests coding agents may be able to diagnose and repair model weight corruption, a possible debugging approach for deployed models.

s9f54670941.title: The Value Semantics Layer: Enabling Machine-Understandable Databases for Agentic AI
s9f54670941.description: arXiv:2611.23629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As data systems increasingly support autonomous LLM-powered agents alongside human analysts, they require richer semantic infrastructure bridging analytical concepts and analytical operations. Existing metadata systems expose schemas, catalogs, lineage, and governance information, but provide limited support for representing operational semantics. We propose the Value Semantics Layer (VSL), an architectural abstraction that externalizes value semantics as persistent, planner-visible infrastructure. VSL introduces Value Semantic Types (VSTs), reusable operational semantic assertions capturing distributional, relational, process, quantitative, and policy-grounded semantics. Unlike descriptive metadata, VSTs enable planners to validate analyti
s9f54670941.summary: Researchers propose the Value Semantics Layer, an architecture that externalizes operational value semantics in databases so LLM agents can plan with them.
s9f54670941.why: Agent-facing databases may need machine-readable operational semantics beyond schemas and lineage, which this architecture proposes to supply.

s1259f1cf62.title: FairPGT: Partitioned Graph Transformers for Dual-Level Fair Graph Clustering
s1259f1cf62.description: arXiv:2611.23631v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clustering on attributed graphs can produce demographically biased clusters, particularly when communities align with protected groups. Graph transformers can amplify this bias through same-group attention, while global attention limits scalability. We propose FairPGT, a partitioned graph transformer for fair graph clustering. FairPGT restricts attention to METIS partitions and connects them through routing tokens, which divides the quadratic cost of attention by the number of partitions. A graph-aware self-training target guides clustering, with a provably bounded deviation from the standard DEC target. Fairness is imposed at two levels: a mutual-information term promotes demographic parity in cluster assignments, while a normalized cross-
s1259f1cf62.summary: Researchers propose FairPGT, a partitioned graph transformer that restricts attention to METIS partitions to reduce bias and cost in fair graph clustering.
s1259f1cf62.why: Offers a way to reduce demographic bias in graph clustering while cutting attention cost, relevant to teams building fairness-sensitive graph pipelines.

s834e9b493e.title: Toaster: Nonlinear Memory from Cascaded Linear Memories and Target Propagation
s834e9b493e.description: arXiv:2611.23648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recurrent memories let language models process long sequences with a fixed-size state. Linear memories such as DeltaNet and KDA store one matrix and take one delta-rule step per token. The product of a chunk of such steps has an exact WY form, so they train fast.
