Deep memories such as TTT-MLP and Titans store a small MLP, which can hold maps that no matrix can, but their update has no WY form. Toaster bridges the two by building on a known fact: a gradient step on a linear layer is a delta-rule write. It builds a two-layer nonlinear memory from two linear memories with an activation between them. We use target propagation to give the hidden memory its values by projecting the output error back through the second memory. Given a chunk's cros
s834e9b493e.summary: Toaster proposes a nonlinear memory built from cascaded linear memories and target propagation, aiming to combine fast training of linear memories with deeper expressivity.
s834e9b493e.why: Could offer language models a long-sequence memory that trains efficiently while holding nonlinear mappings, relevant to architecture choices.

s4bdd3c3bad.title: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates
s4bdd3c3bad.description: arXiv:2611.23651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kicker is a personal health assistant. Changes to an assistant's reusable instructions can improve task handling while changing what it discloses, which requests it follows, and how it reports actions. We study Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation component developed for Kicker. We restrict recursive self-improvement (RSI) to prompt updates, with model weights and runtime code fixed. The procedure tests proposed and current instructions, repeats failing cases, temporarily undoes changes to guide repairs, and checks safety and task performance before adoption. If no version passes, the current instructions stay in use. Our executable benchmark contains 29 email, calendar, health, and marketplace cases, with separate probes for authorizati
s4bdd3c3bad.summary: Researchers study Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation procedure for a personal health assistant that restricts self-improvement to prompt changes and checks safety after updates.
s4bdd3c3bad.why: Shows that prompt-only self-improvement can silently change disclosure and safety behavior, so update evaluation is needed before deployment.

s9a580f9399.title: Lodestone: Automated Semantic Discovery of Datacenter Hardware Specialization
s9a580f9399.description: arXiv:2611.23663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hardware specialization can improve datacenter efficiency. Unfortunately, identifying computations that justify dedicated hardware is difficult. Existing approaches analyze hot functions, instruction patterns, or overheads such as datacenter tax. They can miss fine-grained computations whose aggregate cost is spread across applications and libraries, especially when different pieces of code obscure the same underlying computation. We observe that seemingly unrelated code regions often perform the same computations, creating specialization opportunities that require semantic reasoning. The rise of agentic AI makes it possible to automate this. However, conventional AI agents cannot efficiently and reliably analyze large scale datacenter soft
s9a580f9399.summary: Researchers present Lodestone, an automated method for finding fine-grained computations across datacenter code that justify dedicated hardware specialization.
s9a580f9399.why: Gives infrastructure teams a systematic way to find shared computations worth accelerating, beyond hot-function profiling.

se0d65d858e.title: Communicative On-Policy Distillation: Distilling Black-Box Teacher Capabilities through Communication for Long-Horizon Tasks
se0d65d858e.description: arXiv:2611.23673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is a powerful paradigm for improving language-model agents on long-horizon tasks, yet its conventional formulation relies on teacher logits that text-only black- box models do not expose. To address this limitation, we introduce Communicative On-Policy Distillation (COPD), which uses natural-language communication as a medium for distilling a stronger model's capabilities into a smaller student. During task execution, the student au- tonomously decides when to consult a black-box teacher and formulates open-ended natural- language requests without predefined question templates or intervention schedules. Successful student-teacher interactions are retained as privileged references to supervise fresh adviser-free
se0d65d858e.summary: Researchers introduce Communicative On-Policy Distillation, where a student agent consults a black-box teacher through natural language to learn long-horizon task skills.
se0d65d858e.why: Enables distilling capabilities from API-only teacher models that do not expose logits, relevant to training smaller agents.

s06d6b95479.title: Structured Extraction of Diffraction Data from Covalent Organic Frameworks
s06d6b95479.description: arXiv:2611.23680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is the primary structural evidence for covalent organic frameworks (COFs) and many other materials. Yet decades of measured patterns exist only as images in published figures. Automatic recovery is difficult, because PXRD figures vary widely in format, from a single curve to crowded stacks with labels, insets, and neighboring plots that challenge traditional computer vision. This work presents a pipeline in which a vision large language model (LLM) interprets the layout of each figure, locating the diffraction plot and its curves and sketching a coarse trace of each, while classical computer vision (CV) refines every trace to pixel-level accuracy. Applied to 3,954 COF articles, the pipeline produces 11,445 ca
s06d6b95479.summary: Researchers present a pipeline where a vision LLM extracts powder X-ray diffraction data from published figures of covalent organic frameworks into structured form.
s06d6b95479.why: Shows vision LLMs can recover structured scientific data from figures, useful for teams building literature-mining pipelines.

s7b8728be7b.title: MEM-STRESS: Longitudinal Field Study of a Wearable-Informed AI Chatbot for Stress Management
s7b8728be7b.description: arXiv:2611.23691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stress is an increasingly prevalent concern, creating a need for accessible and personalized support. Stress-management chatbots primarily rely on what users report, which may not capture their physiological changes. Wearables capture these changes, but chatbots rarely use them as memory across conversations. We therefore present MEM-STRESS, a stress-support chatbot that turns a wearable ring's physiological data into a layered memory of daily records, baseline deviations, LLM-generated summaries, and uses it to drive multi-session conversations grounded in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT). In a four-week, non-randomized study with 60 adults, we compared MEM-STRESS (Treatment) with a chatbot remembering only past conversations (Control).
s7b8728be7b.summary: Researchers present MEM-STRESS, a stress-support chatbot that uses a wearable ring's physiological data as layered memory to drive multi-session conversations, and report a longitudinal field study.
s7b8728be7b.why: It shows how wearable sensor data can serve as persistent memory for LLM applications, a pattern relevant to health-oriented product design.

se4f78caa39.title: Rational Ensemble Logic for Cohort Discovery with Real-World Electrophysiology Data
se4f78caa39.description: arXiv:2611.23708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Biomedical knowledge representation should make the passage from observations to conclusions transparent, rigorous, understandable, explainable, and reproducible (TRUER). We introduce Rational Ensemble Logic (QEL) for specifying temporal phenotypes in real-world electrophysiology data (RWED), with a meaning independent of the implementation software. QEL combines three parameterized modal operators (exact displacement, bounded existence, and bounded universality) over rational time with Boolean connectives and first-order quantification. Its Labeled Interval Ensemble (LINE) semantics represents annotated records as finite interval ensembles. We relate the operators to morphological operations and develop endpoint-array algorithms and finite
se4f78caa39.summary: Researchers introduce Rational Ensemble Logic (QEL), a formal logic for specifying temporal phenotypes in real-world electrophysiology data to support cohort discovery.

s521d32807b.title: Learning through Discernment: when a small language model learns from user feedback on the job, and when it decays
s521d32807b.description: arXiv:2611.23716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models on devices could keep improving by learning, overnight, from their own daily work. Without a true outcome, however, something must decide which attempts are worth learning from, and both the model's own judgment and the user's reaction can be wrong. We study a small model (Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B) with a LoRA adapter, fine-tuned each night on the attempts a judge accepts, over 127 lives of up to a year on WebShop and $\tau^2$-bench. We compare the true outcome, the user's stated verdict and the model's own judgment with a separate, frozen "feedback sense" that reads the user's reaction, built in three versions. Judging itself, the model improved and then decayed, over a year and whatever its adapter. A sense that took poli
s521d32807b.summary: A study finds a small on-device language model (Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B) with LoRA adapters can learn nightly from user feedback, but learning quality depends on which feedback signal is trusted and can decay.
s521d32807b.why: It highlights risks of self-training small on-device models on unverified judgments, relevant to teams building continual-learning features.

s5bc18fbd98.title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
s5bc18fbd98.description: arXiv:2611.23728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise event-driven and energy-efficient vision, yet existing spiking vision transformers (S-ViTs) largely confine spiking tokens to fixed and uniform firing schemes along the temporal, spatial and channel dimensions, whereas suppressing the computational redundancy thus incurred calls for adaptive firing mechanisms that operate jointly across all three axes at test time. To this end, we propose the Adaptive Efficient Integrate-and-Fire (AdaE-IF) model, which consults the attention score of each spiking token and routes salient regions to fine-grained firing patterns while assigning energy-frugal coarse patterns to the remaining regions. Building on AdaE-IF, we further introduce Spiking Gated Self-Attention (
s5bc18fbd98.summary: Researchers propose AdaE-IF, an adaptive integrate-and-fire model that routes spiking tokens across time, space and channels at test time for more energy-efficient spiking vision transformers.

s1d61f74c9e.title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow
s1d61f74c9e.description: arXiv:2611.23729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Growing uncertainty in power system operations from renewables integration, extreme weather, and data center loads challenges the reliability of traditional power flow solvers at scale. Machine learning-based proxies are a potentially promising alternative, but the prohibitive cost of generating training data for large grids makes out-of-distribution generalization a key capability for deployment; currently, models trained on small grids lack that capability. In this work, we systematically evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training, and perturbation-based data augmentation improve the zero-shot transfer of three graph neural network-based power flow models from smaller systems to a larger, unseen 500-bus system. We find that
s1d61f74c9e.summary: Researchers evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training and related methods affect out-of-distribution generalization of neural AC power flow models trained on small grids.
s1d61f74c9e.why: Grid operators need ML solvers that generalize to larger, changing grids; the study addresses a key deployment barrier.

s3c38204f27.title: Reliability is a user-specific property of large language models
s3c38204f27.description: arXiv:2611.23732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Public benchmarks support comparisons of large language model (LLM) capabilities, yet users can experience the same highly ranked model differently. Drawing on traditional software reliability, we argue that the reliability of an LLM service should be assessed for specified users and conditions of use. This requires more than a capability score: evaluation evidence must support a claim about failure during future operation. We distinguish testing to discover faults from testing to assess reliability and identify ten modelling considerations behind such claims. We propose a six-workstream research roadmap linking claim specification, dynamic operational profiles, graded outcomes and noisy judgements, local probabilistic robustness, interacti
s3c38204f27.summary: A position paper argues that LLM reliability should be assessed for specific users and conditions of use, not just through general capability benchmarks, and identifies ten modelling considerations.
s3c38204f27.why: Teams deploying LLMs should evaluate reliability against their own users and conditions rather than relying on public leaderboard rankings.

se867850d76.title: Beyond Replacement: Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models
se867850d76.description: arXiv:2611.23750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer a flexible alternative to autoregressive models, enabling any-order infilling. While most existing decoding methods treat decoded tokens as fixed, some recent models allow previously decoded tokens to be revised only by replacing them with alternative tokens, a paradigm we refer to as replacement-only editing (ROE). Although ROE can correct individual tokens, it is inefficient for sequence shifts caused by missing or extra tokens and struggles when errors occur across many positions. To address these limitations, we propose LED (Levenshtein Editing for Diffusion Language Models), a post-training framework that extends ROE with insertion and deletion, enabling Levenshtein-style refinement of generated s
se867850d76.summary: Researchers propose Levenshtein editing for diffusion language models, going beyond replacement-only token revision to handle insertions and deletions that shift sequences.

s39c9f6f805.title: Interpreting Timestamp Permutations in Dynamic Link Prediction
s39c9f6f805.description: arXiv:2611.23753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Timestamp permutations are used to test whether dynamic link predictors exploit temporal information, but a performance gap can reflect changes in training, evaluation history, or both. We separate these effects with a crossed diagnostic and measure input exposure: whether altered histories actually change the predictor's inputs. On MOOC, TCL trained with binary cross-entropy gains approximately eight pairwise-accuracy points from original-chronology training under either evaluation history, while changing history at fixed weights gives only 0.03 points. The small history contrast reflects unchanged inputs for 68.37% of queries, stable rankings for most others, and cancellation of gains and losses. Under original evaluation history, suppres
s39c9f6f805.summary: Researchers use a crossed diagnostic to separate the effects of training and evaluation history on timestamp-permutation tests of dynamic link prediction models.
s39c9f6f805.why: It clarifies when benchmark gaps in temporal models reflect true use of time information versus changes in training or evaluation setup.

s4083725fc8.title: Learning Martial Arts Motion Skills for Animating Opponents in VR Sparring Games
s4083725fc8.description: arXiv:2611.23825v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Animating virtual opponents is an important yet challenging task in game development. In martial arts games, opponent motions must not only be physically plausible but also exhibit appropriate technique, timing, transitions, and target-directed intent. Traditional game animations often rely on handcrafted clips, state machine transitions, and procedural adjustments, which can be labor-intensive and may limit the behavioral diversity of non-player characters. This paper presents a martial arts motion skills learning framework for character animation in virtual sparring games. Inspired by Tang Soo Do, we collected a martial arts motion capture dataset containing isolated attacking and defending techniques, technique combinations and transitio
s4083725fc8.summary: Researchers present a framework that learns martial arts motion skills so virtual opponents in VR sparring games can be animated with physically plausible, target-directed behavior.

s424cff3268.title: TOGBench: Benchmarking and Improving Tiny-Object Generation Fidelity in Aerial Imagery
s424cff3268.description: arXiv:2611.23840v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Advances in deep generative models now enable the synthesis of realistic imagery. However, aerial imagery is dominated by tiny objects, such as vehicles, ships, and aircraft, which occupy only a few pixels owing to the overhead, wide-area nature of aerial imaging. Existing generative models struggle substantially more with tiny objects than with larger ones. This limitation has been overlooked, as prior work on generative evaluation emphasizes prompt following or human preference rather than whether small objects are rendered faithfully. To address this gap, we introduce TOGBench, a quantitative, object-level benchmark for evaluating tiny-object generation fidelity in aerial imagery. We further propose two simple train-/inference-time techn
s424cff3268.summary: Researchers introduce TOGBench, a benchmark measuring how faithfully generative models render tiny objects such as vehicles and ships in aerial imagery, plus methods to improve it.
s424cff3268.why: Generative models often fail on small objects, so teams using synthetic aerial data should check fidelity on tiny objects, not just overall quality.

s28f4147f7d.title: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
s28f4147f7d.description: arXiv:2611.23843v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation, yet their performance often degrades on long-horizon tasks that require multiple interdependent manipulations. Instead of burdening the VLA policies with long-horizon reasoning, memory, action generation, progress tracking, and error recovery, we argue for leveraging their short-horizon manipulation capabilities within an execution-aware framework. To this end, we introduce \textnormal{\textbf{RePlan-VLA}}, a VLA-agnostic framework that translates a VLA's short-horizon capabilities into reliable long-horizon execution. RePlan-VLA explicitly monitors the robot's motion for progress evaluation, and adaptively revises the future p
s28f4147f7d.summary: Researchers introduce RePlan-VLA, a VLA-agnostic framework that adds progress-aware replanning and error recovery to vision-language-action models for long-horizon robotic manipulation.
s28f4147f7d.why: Wrapping existing VLA policies with execution-aware replanning offers a way to improve long-horizon robot tasks without retraining the base model.

s25c45b0498.title: ReflectScene:MLLM-Guided Closed-Loop Diffusion for 3D Indoor Scene Generation
s25c45b0498.description: arXiv:2611.23845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-conditioned 3D indoor scene generation requires layouts satisfying geometric, functional, and semantic constraints. However, existing diffusion methods rely primarily on static textual conditions, limiting their ability to assess evolving scenes and translate semantic discrepancies into executable object-level corrections. MLLM-based post-hoc refinement provides semantic feedback but remains decoupled from denoising, potentially disrupting scene coherence.We propose ReflectScene, an MLLM-guided closed-loop diffusion framework. First, we introduce Hierarchical Prior-Grounded Scene Understanding that aligns structured layouts with multi-view visual evidence, to interpret object-specific context and scene global semantics via a frozen mul
s25c45b0498.summary: Researchers propose ReflectScene, a closed-loop diffusion framework where an MLLM gives feedback during denoising to generate more coherent text-conditioned 3D indoor scenes.

s6426fc24a6.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
s6426fc24a6.description: arXiv:2611.23858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Grasping is a fundamental capability for robotic manipulation, with the appropriate grasp depending on the downstream task. For example, a hammer should be held by its handle for hammering but by its head when it is handed over. Selecting such a grasp requires consideration of two criteria: physical feasibility on the object and suitability for the task. Developing such an approach requires dense grasp labels with both feasibility and task scores on real observations, but existing task-oriented grasping datasets are small, synthetic, or costly to annotate. To address this gap, we construct a dataset of 2.68 million scored 5-DoF grasp annotations over 100,911 image-task pairs from $17$ object categories. Additionally, we introduce LAGR, a ta
s6426fc24a6.summary: Researchers present LAGR, a language-aware method that re-ranks robotic grasps for task-oriented grasping, combining physical feasibility with task suitability.

scf177cfc08.title: Grounding Radiology Reports in 3D Chest CT: Results of the ReXGrounding Challenge
scf177cfc08.description: arXiv:2611.23862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Segmenting each reported finding in a radiology scan would allow findings to be measured and tracked over time and let AI systems generate reports that are verifiable, but so far AI models have performed poorly at this task. To advance this task, we organized the ReXGrounding Challenge at MICCAI 2026, the first challenge dedicated to it. Given a non-contrast chest CT scan and the set of findings from its report, participants trained models to produce the corresponding set of 3D segmentations. The challenge used 2,992 training and 200 validation scans from the ReXGroundingCT dataset, and evaluated methods on a held-out test set of 300 scans with 582 findings, exhaustively annotated by board-certified radiologists. In total, 48 teams from 15
scf177cfc08.summary: Results are reported from the ReXGrounding Challenge at MICCAI, where participants trained models to segment radiology report findings in 3D chest CT scans, using 2,992 training and 200 validation cases.
scf177cfc08.why: Verifiable AI radiology reports depend on grounding findings in images, and this challenge benchmarks progress on a task where models have performed poorly.

s0ad3a10b63.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents
s0ad3a10b63.description: arXiv:2611.23875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical neural networks promise fast, energy-efficient computing, but every device departs from its design and must be trained with the hardware. In situ training relies on an expert-built calibrated digital model of each device or on gradient-free trial and error. Coding agents, large language models that write and run programs, have shown an emergent ability to understand and edit the weights of digital neural networks. Here we introduce optics as code, a method in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from measurements alone, through a harness that returns camera images of its probes and requires a hypothesis per request. We discovered that the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the netw
s0ad3a10b63.summary: Researchers introduce optics as code, in which a coding agent trains an optical neural network from hardware measurements alone, without a calibrated digital model of the device.
s0ad3a10b63.why: Using coding agents to train physical hardware from measurements could cut the expert effort needed for in situ optical computing.

s273ce5e5c4.title: NullTok: empirical-null token selection for training-free long video understanding
s273ce5e5c4.description: arXiv:2611.23881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long video understanding remains a daunting challenge for existing multimodal large language models (MLLMs), mainly due to the large number of visual tokens accumulated in long videos. Currently, frame selection and token selection are two main paradigms for addressing this issue, both aiming to select relevant visual information to form a compact input for MLLMs. A natural approach combines these two paradigms by selecting frames before pruning tokens, but noisy frame-level relevance estimates can cause irreversible evidence loss. In this paper, we study this problem from the perspective of assessing the spatiotemporal distribution of query-specific evidence and propose a novel and training-free approach termed NULLTOK. For every patch acr
s273ce5e5c4.summary: Researchers propose NullTok, a training-free method that selects visual tokens using an empirical-null approach for long video understanding in multimodal LLMs.
s273ce5e5c4.why: It offers a training-free way to shrink visual inputs for long videos, potentially cutting compute without retraining models.

sa1a23415b6.title: SixthView: A Benchmark for Hidden-View Reconstruction and 3D Assembly Reasoning
sa1a23415b6.description: arXiv:2611.23891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inferring the unseen side of a 3D assembly requires reasoning about part placement and occlusion. Different assemblies can match the observed views while producing different hidden views, leaving the target ambiguous. We introduce SixthView, a benchmark in which models predict a sixth orthographic view from five observed views and information about the component shapes. The benchmark contains 602 synthetic polycube assemblies with 2--10 parts and requires a dense grid of part labels for the missing view, allowing both exact-view and cell-level evaluation. For each item, we exhaustively verify that all legal assemblies consistent with the exact component geometry and observed label grids yield the same target view. With these inputs, the tas
sa1a23415b6.summary: Researchers introduce SixthView, a benchmark of 602 synthetic polycube assemblies where models predict a hidden sixth orthographic view from five observed views.

s473f8a7484.title: Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting
s473f8a7484.description: arXiv:2611.23896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kernel Ridge Attention (KRA) is a recurrent sequence mixer that combines learned nonlinear features with covariance-guided memory updates. It stores associations through recursive ridge regression, using correlations among past keys to determine how new observations modify memory. A content-dependent Ornstein--Uhlenbeck transition controls retention and restores uncertainty for future writes. This construction admits an exact temporal-kernel interpretation and maintains an inference state whose size is independent of context length. Associative block maps and explicit adjoints support parallel training while preserving the recursive update. In controlled language-modeling experiments, KRA improves prediction quality over attention and recur
s473f8a7484.summary: Researchers present Kernel Ridge Attention, a recurrent sequence mixer with nonlinear features and covariance-guided memory updates whose inference state size is independent of context length.
s473f8a7484.why: A constant-size inference state independent of context length could matter for long-sequence architectures, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

s2566aca05d.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
s2566aca05d.description: arXiv:2611.23930v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are expected to achieve semantic reasoning, intelligent decision-making, and long-horizon navigation under strict onboard constraints. While recent foundation-model-driven approaches have shown promising progress toward this goal, existing methods remain limited by challenges in 3D data availability, trajectory feasibility, long-horizon reasoning, and computational efficiency in complex environments. To bridge these gaps, we propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation (VLN) framework for aerial robots. VLN-AR decouples multimodal reasoning and low-level control, enabling structured prediction of 3D pose commands and navigation intentions that are translated into dynamically feasible actions. To
s2566aca05d.summary: Researchers propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation framework for aerial robots designed to run under strict onboard constraints in complex environments.
s2566aca05d.why: It targets onboard semantic navigation for UAVs under compute limits, relevant to teams building embodied or robotics systems.

s1460038600.title: Angular Conditional Distillation: Overcoming Classifier Geometry Mismatch
s1460038600.description: arXiv:2611.23941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classifier outputs provide a fundamental and univer- sally available knowledge interface for knowledge distil- lation (KD). However, standard logit objectives entangle transferable semantic relations with architecture-dependent parameterization artifacts, causing a classifier geometry mismatch that makes direct knowledge transfer unreliable. To address this, we propose Angular Conditional Distilla- tion (ACD). First, the Angular Coordinate Interface (ACI) reconstructs the student classifier using angular coordi- nates, suppressing magnitude and bias effects to provide a geometry-compatible space. Then, Scale-Invariant Condi- tional Distillation (SICD) standardizes outputs and exclu- sively transfers conditional non-target relations, filteri
s1460038600.summary: Researchers propose Angular Conditional Distillation, which uses angular coordinates for classifier outputs to address geometry mismatch in knowledge distillation between models.
s1460038600.why: Better logit-based distillation across different architectures could improve transferring knowledge from large models into smaller deployed ones.

s69bf33f377.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?
s69bf33f377.description: arXiv:2611.23946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents are widely trained in executable GUI environments. To lower cost, build environments in batches, and reduce manual effort, each work trades away part of the environment through its construction choices. We describe these choices along three dimensions: reward coverage, the goal-reaching trajectories the verifier rewards; data coverage, the application data the agent is exposed to beyond what the task reads or writes; and feature coverage, the application features beyond what the task uses. Existing works set each dimension on engineering grounds, but they do not measure its effect on training. How complete must an environment be to train a capable agent, and along which dimensions? In MobileGym, we adju
s69bf33f377.summary: Researchers analyze how completely GUI environments must cover rewards, data, and features to train capable GUI agents, framing tradeoffs across three coverage dimensions.
s69bf33f377.why: It gives guidance on how much environment fidelity is needed when building cheaper training environments for computer-use agents.

s8d208142b4.title: SEE: Unlocking the Hidden Perception of Frozen VLMs
s8d208142b4.description: arXiv:2611.23962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) grasp the overall content of an image but often miss the fine details a question hinges on, such as a small object in a large photo or a number in a dense infographic. Yet even when their answer is wrong, the region they point to often contains the evidence. We introduce Self-Elicited Evidence (SEE), a training-free method that lets a frozen VLM look again where it points. When the initial answer has low confidence, SEE prompts the model to propose regions where the details may appear, answers the question on these enlarged crops, and aggregates the answers with the original prediction through confidence-weighted voting. The model also answers with its own transcript, which helps on text-rich images. SEE needs
s8d208142b4.summary: Researchers introduce Self-Elicited Evidence (SEE), a training-free method that makes frozen vision-language models re-examine regions they point to when answer confidence is low.
s8d208142b4.why: A training-free way to improve fine-detail answers from frozen VLMs can be applied without fine-tuning or extra training cost.

sd4d0f7eb76.title: Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders
sd4d0f7eb76.description: arXiv:2611.23964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In latent diffusion models, expanding the latent dimension of variational autoencoders (VAEs) is essential to push the upper bound of reconstruction quality. However, without explicit structural constraints, such unregularized expansion easily yields a rugged and ill-conditioned latent manifold, causing generated latents to drift off the manifold during generation (i.e., off-manifold problem). Recent works smooth this manifold by using external foundation models (e.g., DINOv2) as a topological regularizer. However, we argue that tying the latent space to frozen external priors inherently restricts generalization: bound by their pre-training distributions and semantic biases, they may fail to capture faithful visual details on out-of-distrib
sd4d0f7eb76.summary: Researchers propose Dual-Manifold Variational Autoencoders to address off-manifold drift in latent diffusion models when VAE latent dimensions are expanded.

s98cfcda37f.title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting
s98cfcda37f.description: arXiv:2611.23970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Forecasting future hand movements from egocentric videos plays an important role in understanding human intentions and hand-object interactions. However, different manipulation intentions can lead to substantially different hand trajectories even when interacting with the same object. Existing methods have not sufficiently explored the intrinsic relationships between articulated hand movements and object semantics to capture such operation-dependent motion patterns. Therefore, we propose TOMAS, a topology-aware operation modeling and adaptive staging framework for egocentric hand forecasting. Specifically, we develop a topology-aware hand-object reasoning mechanism that associates hand skeletal structures and articulation dynamics with obje
s98cfcda37f.summary: Researchers present TOMAS, a topology-aware method for forecasting egocentric hand movements by modeling operation-dependent motion patterns tied to object semantics.

s100ef8b279.title: ReliFlow: Reliability-Calibrated Residual Transport for Combinatorial Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
s100ef8b279.description: arXiv:2611.23999v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting the transcriptional response to combined perturbations requires distinguishing interactions between interventions from errors in their individual effect estimates. The latter become more pronounced when single-perturbation evidence is sparse or withheld. We introduce a conditional flow-matching model that estimates the reliability of single-gene effects from training-only cross-fitting and uses those estimates to calibrate the additive source distribution. The velocity is decomposed into a known correction of the additive reference and a learned residual transport field. On Norman genetic perturbations, reduces mean absolute error (MAE) from 0.142 to 0.131 for unseen combinations of observed singles and from 0.198 to 0.178 when c
s100ef8b279.summary: Researchers introduce ReliFlow, a conditional flow-matching model that calibrates single-gene effect reliability to predict combinatorial single-cell perturbation responses.

s2d90191ae0.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
s2d90191ae0.description: arXiv:2611.24000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can infer and follow specific rules through in-context learning (ICL), yet may fail to remain faithful to provided evidence, giving rise to out-of-context (OOC) hallucination. Existing work has largely investigated the underlying mechanisms of ICL and OOC hallucination along separate lines. However, this separation obscures the mechanistic basis for these seemingly opposing outcomes. In this work, we study this contrast through the unified view of functional roles in dynamic context. The key observation is that role information can be internally represented without reliably constraining output. We derive a first-order decomposition to characterize the role effect, showing that its substantial influence depends on two n
s2d90191ae0.summary: Researchers present a mechanistic analysis linking in-context learning and out-of-context hallucination in LLMs through the functional roles of tokens in dynamic context.
s2d90191ae0.why: Understanding the shared mechanisms behind in-context rule following and unfaithful hallucination could inform more reliable LLM behavior.

s3d9aff4e6f.title: Rethinking Fixed-Horizon Latent Reasoning
s3d9aff4e6f.description: arXiv:2611.24001v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing latent reasoners typically run for a preset latent horizon during inference. Intuitively, a longer horizon should provide more opportunity for reasoning. However, in this work, we find that extending latent Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to the full preset horizon may in fact degrade reasoning performance. We observe that latent CoT evolves through distinct functional stages, with earlier computation forming frontier reasoning states, while later computation mainly reorganizes existing candidates and can weaken gold candidate support. These findings motivate a rethink of fixed-horizon latent inference. To address this, we characterize the reasoning benefits of latent CoT by realized and remaining constructive progress. Empirically, we find
s3d9aff4e6f.summary: Researchers find that running latent chain-of-thought for the full preset horizon can degrade reasoning, as later computation reorganizes candidates and weakens gold support.
s3d9aff4e6f.why: Fixed-length latent reasoning may hurt accuracy, suggesting inference budgets for latent reasoners should be tuned rather than maximized.

se2f279b4ae.title: ProtoBridge-CLIP: Observation-Masked Finding Prototypes for Medical Image--Report Representation Learning
se2f279b4ae.description: arXiv:2611.24002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiology reports distinguish affirmed findings, explicit negations, and unmentioned concepts, but conventional global image--report contrastive learning often compresses these different evidence states into a single study-level target. We introduce \model{}, which combines symmetric global image--report alignment with observation-masked finding supervision and a soft relation objective over affirmed report concepts. Text-derived finding prototypes are aligned with local visual tokens, while uncertain and unmentioned concepts are excluded from direct finding labels. We evaluate the framework on three CT benchmarks and five chest-radiograph benchmarks, together with component ablations, paired and clinical retrieval, localization, perturbati
se2f279b4ae.summary: Researchers introduce ProtoBridge-CLIP, which aligns text-derived finding prototypes with local visual tokens while excluding uncertain and unmentioned concepts for medical image-report learning.

sfed4709d09.title: Choosing Supervised Post-Processing for Frozen Person Detectors: Information, Object Changes, and Complete Cost
sfed4709d09.description: arXiv:2611.24003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen detector computes hypotheses that can support better final outputs through supervised post-processing. Choosing a readout requires knowing which available information improves detection and what its processing costs. We compare candidate scores, class distributions, geometry, native-set summaries and adapted neighborhood meta classification under common candidate, supervision and operating-point conditions. On 320 held-out CrowdHuman images, adding native-set context to a 97-dimensional readout yields 275 more matches and 96 more unmatched predictions. On a separate 319-image cohort, Full100 matches 6004 objects,versus 5848 for source-selected raw WBF and 6002 for a MetaDetect-style adaptation. Its gain over raw contains 300 added
sfed4709d09.summary: Researchers compare supervised post-processing readouts for frozen person detectors on 320 CrowdHuman images, weighing information gains against complete processing costs.
sfed4709d09.why: Shows that adding native-set context to a detector readout can yield more matches, informing cost-aware post-processing choices in detection pipelines.

sdaaae59d27.title: How Reward Gain Imbalance Shapes Ranking: Rethinking Rubric-Based Reward Aggregation
sdaaae59d27.description: arXiv:2611.24005v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rubric-based reinforcement learning constructs rewards for aligning large language models with human preferences, typically by equally aggregating continuous scores that a judge assigns to individual criteria. However, scoring heterogeneity across criteria can distort candidate rankings. Existing work has focused on improving judges, learning criterion weights, or refining aggregation, whereas the interaction between scoring heterogeneity and ranking remains insufficiently understood. We formalize this heterogeneity as \emph{reward gain imbalance}: each criterion enters the aggregated reward with its own reward gain, the gap between its expected scores on satisfied and unsatisfied responses. Counterintuitively, our experiments show that rem
sdaaae59d27.summary: Researchers formalize reward gain imbalance in rubric-based reinforcement learning, showing how uneven criterion scoring heterogeneity can distort candidate rankings for LLM alignment.
sdaaae59d27.why: Equal aggregation of rubric scores can silently skew rankings in RL alignment pipelines, so reward design choices affect outcomes.

s26c2dc6940.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
s26c2dc6940.description: arXiv:2611.24025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a re
s26c2dc6940.summary: Researchers propose intent contracts, an authorization design where the planning LLM holds no tools and a trusted model writes each tool call after checking a logged contract.
s26c2dc6940.why: Offers a concrete pattern for limiting what tool-using agents can do, with logged, validated authorization before any action runs.

s23cb1a516f.title: FormalFixer: Intent-Aligned Automated Hardware Repair via Joint Refinement of Specifications, Assertions, and RTL Implementations
s23cb1a516f.description: arXiv:2611.24037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Functional errors in hardware designs can compromise correctness and security, and must be fixed before tape-out. Formal property verification (FPV) provides strong guarantees by proving or refuting assertions, but a failed assertion is not always evidence of an RTL defect: the failure may also come from a buggy assertion or from a specification that is semantically correct but too ambiguous or incomplete for direct formalization. This creates a practical repair problem that existing RTL-centric methods do not directly address: the repair loop must align specification intent, verification intent, and RTL behavior before deciding which artifact to change. \textsc{FormalFixer} addresses this problem with a multi-stage, intent-aligned repair w
s23cb1a516f.summary: FormalFixer proposes a method that jointly refines specifications, assertions, and RTL code to repair hardware designs when formal verification assertions fail.
s23cb1a516f.why: Addresses that failed assertions may stem from buggy assertions or ambiguous specs, not only RTL defects, which matters for pre-tape-out verification workflows.

sbba080784a.title: From Data to Valves: A Self-Learning, Production-Grade Edge Stack for Sustainable HVAC Control
sbba080784a.description: arXiv:2611.24052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned HVAC controllers rarely leave the simulator, and those that do are typically trained offline, frozen at deployment and retrained from the cloud. We present a production stack in which three learning components run on one NVIDIA Jetson Orin gateway per building, adapt continuously from the building's own data, and verify their own effect. (a) A compact transformer-encoder forecaster, one per equipment group with learned per-unit embeddings, predicts every air-side unit's next-cycle temperature and learns prequentially, one gradient step per five-minute cycle, behind five independent gates that bound the influence of any corrupt reading. (b) A distributional soft actor-critic agent, one shared policy across unit types, converts the me
sbba080784a.summary: Researchers describe a production HVAC control stack where learning components run on an edge gateway per building, adapting continuously from local data and verifying their own effect.
sbba080784a.why: Shows a deployed pattern for on-premise, continuously adapting learned controllers on edge hardware instead of cloud-retrained frozen models.

sd2a9d714a3.title: Grading Executable Legal Rules Against Independent Records: Transitional Provisions and Korean SME Status
sd2a9d714a3.description: arXiv:2611.24055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laws are increasingly turned into programs that decide cases, such as whether a firm was a small or medium enterprise (SME) on a given date, and large language models (LLMs) now write them. The programs are usually graded against answers written by someone who read the same law, so a program can score well by sharing the grader's reading rather than by getting the law right. LexTemporis grades them instead against records of what actually happened: 10,901 firm-years of SME status disclosed by Korean listed companies, with every version of the governing rules. An appendix adds comparison cases from US income tax and German hospital minimum volumes. The date changes outcomes mainly through provisions outside the main statutory text: one trans
sd2a9d714a3.summary: LexTemporis grades executable legal rules against real records of Korean listed firms' SME status rather than against answers written by someone reading the same law.
sd2a9d714a3.why: Suggests validating LLM-generated rule programs against ground-truth records rather than reviewer interpretations, a useful evaluation approach for compliance logic.

s460d6bf61b.title: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
s460d6bf61b.description: arXiv:2611.24059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the experts' RL runs have already produced what consolidation needs: rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards, in the order the experts learned from them. We propose multi-expert replay policy distillation (MRPD), which replays these training logs through the student in the experts' order. At each step, the policy gradient is recomputed
s460d6bf61b.summary: Researchers propose replaying stored RL rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards to consolidate domain experts, instead of resampling in multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
s460d6bf61b.why: Could cut the cost of consolidating post-training experts into one model by reusing rollouts the experts already produced.

s172f56aa72.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
s172f56aa72.description: arXiv:2611.24077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision.
s172f56aa72.summary: AeroRSI is a recursive self-improvement framework where an aerial vision-language navigation policy learns from its own failures in closed-loop flight.
s172f56aa72.why: Presents a way to generate repair data for drone VLA policies without relying on human pilot labels or rule-based planners.

s93804be1e8.title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
s93804be1e8.description: arXiv:2611.24079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting
s93804be1e8.summary: APS proposes adaptive partitioning for frame selection to improve long video understanding in large vision-language models under computational budgets.
s93804be1e8.why: Offers a method to reduce visual input cost for long-video LVLM pipelines by choosing frames over adaptive temporal regions.

sd8af7bf496.title: LEDGE: An Efficient Simulator for Distributed LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Devices
sd8af7bf496.description: arXiv:2611.24085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating distributed large language model (LLM) serving on heterogeneous edge devices requires exploring diverse model partitions, device placements, and network conditions, making repeated physical experiments costly. An efficient simulator for edge LLM serving must support diverse, fine-grained placement configurations, capture runtime behavior, and accurately predict execution times while keeping simulation overhead low. We present LEDGE, a lightweight simulator for fast, fine-grained evaluation of distributed LLM serving on heterogeneous edge devices without executing tensor operations. LEDGE constructs event graphs supporting non-uniform tensor and pipeline parallelism, estimates execution costs using reusable performance models cali
sd8af7bf496.summary: LEDGE is a lightweight simulator for evaluating distributed LLM serving across heterogeneous edge devices, covering model partitions, device placement, and network conditions.
sd8af7bf496.why: Lets teams explore edge LLM deployment configurations without costly physical experiments, though the text gives no performance results.

s1327220237.title: The 7th International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026): Summary and Results
s1327220237.description: arXiv:2611.24114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This report summarizes the seventh International Verification of Neural Networks Com- petition (VNN-COMP 2026), held as part of the Symposium on AI Verification (SAIV) co-located with the International Conference on Computer-Aided Verification (CAV) at FLoC 2026 in Lisbon, Portugal. The goal of the competition is to provide an objective comparison of the state-of-the-art methods in neural network verification, in terms of scal- ability and speed. Along this line, we used standard formats (ONNX for neural networks and VNNLIB for specifications), standard hardware (all tools are run by the organizers on AWS), and tool parameters provided by the tool authors. This report summarizes the rules, benchmarks, participating tools, results, and lesso
s1327220237.summary: The seventh International Verification of Neural Networks Competition (VNN-COMP 2026) summarized its results, comparing neural network verification methods on scalability and speed.
s1327220237.why: Provides an objective benchmark snapshot of which neural network verification tools currently scale best.

sdbfe58cf56.title: How Well Do Generalist CT Foundation Models Differentiate Liver Tumors?
sdbfe58cf56.description: arXiv:2611.24122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalist CT foundation models detect many findings with high performance, but their ability to differentiate detected lesions remains largely unevaluated. This retrospective study evaluated two generalist models, RADAR and Merlin, for differentiating liver tumors using a public single-institution multiphase CT dataset (517 cases: hepatocellular carcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, breast and colorectal cancer liver metastases, and hemangioma). The models were evaluated in a zero-shot setting using their existing outputs and with linear probing, in which only a linear classifier was trained on frozen image features (stratified fivefold cross-validation repeated five times). In the zero-shot setting, RADAR achieved an accuracy of 54.
sdbfe58cf56.summary: A retrospective study evaluated generalist CT foundation models RADAR and Merlin on differentiating liver tumors across 517 multiphase CT cases.
sdbfe58cf56.why: Shows generalist medical imaging models may detect lesions well but are not established as reliable at differentiating tumor types.

sc6c8f45692.title: Inherited Adapter Experts for Replay-Free Domain-Incremental Learning
sc6c8f45692.description: arXiv:2611.24145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Replay-free domain-incremental learning trains a model on the same classes in successive domains without keeping earlier images. Per-domain learners freeze a pre-trained ViT and train an additional expert for each new domain: the small set of parameters and the classification head learned on that domain. Test images carry no domain label, so a router selects one expert for each image. Recent work trains this router. However, a training-free Mahalanobis router costs the analyzed learners under 2.7 points of final accuracy relative to always selecting each image's own-domain expert. The experts, not this router, limit accuracy. Our learner, Lamarck, therefore uses this router and strengthens the experts. Its adapters, small trainable layers t
sc6c8f45692.summary: Researchers study replay-free domain-incremental learning with adapter experts and a training-free Mahalanobis router that selects an expert per image without domain labels.
sc6c8f45692.why: Shows a training-free routing option for continual learning that trades a small amount of accuracy for simpler deployment.

sf4db0dde45.title: Once Upon a Bias: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories
sf4db0dde45.description: arXiv:2611.24156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to create stories for children. Since bedtime stories can shape children's perceptions of social roles, this raises concerns about whether LLMs adapt narrative portrayals according to the intended recipient's gender. We conducted a large-scale study to examine gender stereotyping in LLM-generated bedtime stories. Using matched daughter/son prompts and a five-generation design, we analyze 62,873 retained stories from 16 LLMs across 35 country settings and 12 narrator roles. We introduce a multi-level evaluation framework combining context-adjusted lexical rate contrasts, relative stereotype alignment, narrator-recipient interaction analysis, human evaluation, and representation-level interventions
sf4db0dde45.summary: A large-scale study of 62,873 LLM-generated bedtime stories from 16 models finds analysis of gender stereotyping tied to whether the intended recipient is a daughter or son.
sf4db0dde45.why: Highlights measurable gender bias in LLM content for children, relevant to teams shipping generative storytelling or education products.

se4df014173.title: Gaussian Primitive Fusion for Any-Resolution Multimodal Images
se4df014173.description: arXiv:2611.24164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal image fusion integrates complementary observations from different modalities into a unified representation. Existing methods typically estimate modality contributions on a common discrete grid. When source modalities have different native resolutions, constructing such a grid generally involves resampling, which may introduce artifacts and affect subsequent fusion decisions. To address this problem, we propose Gaussian Primitive Fusion (GPF), which reformulates heterogeneous-resolution fusion in a shared continuous Gaussian space. Instead of first converting source images to a common resolution, GPF directly fits their native-resolution observations with shared Gaussian geometry and modality-specific content representations, and
se4df014173.summary: Gaussian Primitive Fusion proposes fusing multimodal images of different native resolutions in a shared continuous Gaussian space instead of resampling to a common grid.
se4df014173.why: Avoids resampling artifacts in heterogeneous-resolution sensor fusion, though the text gives no quantitative results.

sd9a8e9288a.title: CounselTraj: Synthesizing Process-Aware Psychological Counseling Dialogues via Dialogue-Act Trajectory Planning
sd9a8e9288a.description: arXiv:2611.24168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing demand for psychological counseling has motivated the development of LLM-based systems that support human counselors, but training such systems requires large-scale, high-quality dialogue data. Authentic counseling transcripts are difficult to collect and share because of privacy concerns, making synthetic dialogues an important alternative. However, existing synthetic datasets, despite covering diverse scenarios and client profiles, often consist of brief exchanges and fail to capture session-level counseling processes. We propose CounselTraj, a dialogue-act trajectory planning framework for expanding brief synthetic dialogues into process-aware, session-level psychological counseling dialogues. CounselTraj learns dialogue-act
sd9a8e9288a.summary: CounselTraj proposes synthesizing session-level psychological counseling dialogues by planning dialogue-act trajectories, as an alternative to privacy-limited real transcripts.
sd9a8e9288a.why: Offers a privacy-friendly route to session-length training data for counseling systems, though the text gives little on outcomes.

s51a395df86.title: VideoACE: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding through High-Frame-Rate Actions
s51a395df86.description: arXiv:2611.24184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic video understanding requires models to actively interact with video environments to gather evidence and form judgments. Evaluating this capability therefore requires assessing whether models can translate opportunities for interaction into better understanding. We introduce VideoACE, a benchmark for assessing video understanding under conditions that support sustained interaction. We focus on high-frame-rate action videos, where rapid, subtle changes make targeted observation especially valuable. The benchmark comprises 1,000 multiple-choice questions spanning six categories of fine-grained action understanding, accompanied by temporal evidence annotations and user hints screened for answer leakage. Its evaluation environment combin
s51a395df86.summary: VideoACE is a benchmark of 1,000 multiple-choice questions on high-frame-rate action videos for assessing agentic video understanding through sustained interaction.
s51a395df86.why: Gives teams a benchmark for testing whether video agents can turn interaction opportunities into better understanding.

sbd8b61bd4b.title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
sbd8b61bd4b.description: arXiv:2611.24187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. Receding-horizon beam search with online replanning jointly schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and termination (stop), paired with slack-aware shadow pricing and legal fallback at larger budgets
sbd8b61bd4b.summary: Researchers propose a constrained world-model planning method for visual inspection that localizes multiple targets under strict compute and sensing limits.
sbd8b61bd4b.why: Offers a planning approach for robots using frozen detectors under compute and sensing caps, relevant to field robotics teams.

s235113771a.title: SpiderMark: Hybrid Watermarking for Generative AI via Algorithmic Injection and Learning-Based Verification
s235113771a.description: arXiv:2611.24200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The proliferation of diffusion-based generative models has intensified the need for reliable methods to trace and verify the provenance of AI-generated images. Existing watermarking approaches for diffusion models typically rely on isotropic frequency patterns and handcrafted detection metrics, which are prone to directional vulnerability and threshold instability across diverse image transformations. We propose SpiderMark, a hybrid watermarking framework that combines algorithmic frequency-domain injection with learning-based probabilistic verification, requiring no modifications to pretrained diffusion model weights. SpiderMark embeds a structured spider-web pattern, comprising radial spokes and concentric polygonal rings, into the Fourie
s235113771a.summary: SpiderMark is a hybrid watermarking framework for diffusion-generated images that combines frequency-domain injection with learning-based verification.
s235113771a.why: Provides a provenance-tracing method for generated images that aims to be more robust to transformations than handcrafted approaches.

sad08873ba1.title: Conditional What-If Generation for Radio Access Network Energy under Rare and Unseen Contexts
sad08873ba1.description: arXiv:2611.24208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy-saving mechanisms in RANs must balance energy reduction and network performance under varying traffic conditions. Conditional generative models support what-if analysis by generating plausible power-consumption trajectories for radio configurations and operating scenarios, helping operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment. However, representative measurements are costly and operationally constrained, so historical data cover only limited configurations and conditions, leaving some contexts poorly represented or unseen during training. In this paper, we study conditional generation of RAN power-consumption trajectories under decreasing training coverage, from well-represented to rare and unseen configurations. We fir
sad08873ba1.summary: Researchers present conditional generative models for what-if analysis of radio access network energy consumption in rare and unseen operating contexts.
sad08873ba1.why: Shows how generative models could help telecom operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment when measurement data is sparse.

sb83a37376b.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models
sb83a37376b.description: arXiv:2611.24214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling laws are widely used to predict foundation model performance and guide compute allocation. However, tabular foundation models (TFMs) differ from conventional foundation models in that they are pretrained on virtually unlimited synthetic data from configurable distributions, while ultimately being evaluated on real-world datasets. We investigate whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings. Our analysis reveals differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that accurately fitting a scaling law does not necessarily yield reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. In particular, selecting configurations using too few eva
sb83a37376b.summary: A study examines whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style tabular foundation models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and real-world datasets.
sb83a37376b.why: Highlights that synthetic pretraining may make scaling predictions for tabular models unreliable, which matters when planning compute spend.

sb7a81c659a.title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents
sb7a81c659a.description: arXiv:2611.24231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal language models increasingly answer questions over external documents, exposing them to indirect prompt injection: commands planted in untrusted content to hijack the response. Rendering untrusted content as page images lowers attack success on average, leaving open which injected operations survive rendering, at what utility cost, and whether failed image attacks reflect unread commands or commands read but not followed. We pair text and page-image versions of 191 English question-answering sources across six models, measuring marker appending, answer formatting, and answer replacement alongside clean Question-Answering utility. Rendering reduces append and format execution for every model, yet Qwen3-VL-8B still executes image-b
sb7a81c659a.summary: Researchers test which prompt injection attacks survive when untrusted documents are rendered as page images instead of text, across six multimodal models.
sb7a81c659a.why: Shows image rendering reduces some injection risks but not all, informing how teams secure document-QA pipelines.

s4d8e50dff2.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
s4d8e50dff2.description: arXiv:2611.24313v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Prompt injection is the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents, and the community now agrees that robustness must be measured against adaptive attackers rather than fixed benchmark injections. Many adaptive red teamers exist, and most are built to maximize attack success rate (ASR). Yet ASR counts how often a target breaks, not in how many different ways. A red teamer can achieve a high ASR by reusing a few techniques that work, leaving the others untested and absent from the attacks used to harden models. We present AutoPI, an adaptive red teamer designed to find many different ways to break a target, not just to break it often. AutoPI uses PIAtlas, a taxonomy of prompt-injection techniques, both to guide its search and to measure
s4d8e50dff2.summary: AutoPI is an adaptive red-teaming method for LLM agents that uses a attack taxonomy to test prompt injection across many distinct techniques, not just high success rates.
s4d8e50dff2.why: Gives security teams a way to test agents against a wider variety of injection techniques rather than a few effective ones.

s1ab7165b25.title: Fuse to Recognize the Unseen: Class-Relative Infrared-Visible Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
s1ab7165b25.description: arXiv:2611.24316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visible-infrared image fusion leverages complementary thermal cues to enhance visual perception, particularly under challenging illumination. However, such perceptual complementarity does not readily translate into semantic gains in open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS), where CLIP-based models are predominantly pretrained on RGB imagery. Directly introducing IR information may instead disrupt RGB-language alignment, turning promising thermal cues into semantic interference that undermines unseen-class recognition. Our pixel-level RGB-IR semantic analysis reveals that class-relevant thermal cues can correct certain RGB misclassifications while preserving reliable RGB predictions, motivating RGB-anchored, class-relative thermal cue se
s1ab7165b25.summary: Researchers propose a pixel-level RGB-infrared fusion method to improve open-vocabulary semantic segmentation without disrupting CLIP's RGB-language alignment.
s1ab7165b25.why: Suggests a way to add thermal input to CLIP-based segmentation without losing unseen-class recognition.

s6bcdc8c756.title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities?
s6bcdc8c756.description: arXiv:2611.24330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate whether a weight edit can alter how a model trades off honoring a commitment against benefiting more people. In a concept-supervised text model, we alter fitted choice weights so that the benefit required to override a formal pledge is larger than for an ordinary promise. Across six independently trained text readers, the edit selects the larger group in both orders on 100% of targeted ordinary conflicts and 83.3% of targeted formal conflicts. It preserves the source model's success rates on smaller conflicts and its factual accuracy. The remaining formal-conflict failures coincide with errors reading a beneficiary number. A separate classifier demonstrates why this distinction matters: reusing a factual answer passes an unco
s6bcdc8c756.summary: Researchers show a weight edit in a concept-supervised text model can change how it trades off honoring a formal pledge against benefiting more people.
s6bcdc8c756.why: Demonstrates that model-level ethical trade-offs can be altered by weight edits, a concern for alignment and auditing.

sa48f07ba41.title: OCTR2A: Real-Time RGB-to-BEV Trajectory Projection and Forecasting at Urban Intersections
sa48f07ba41.description: arXiv:2611.24352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trajectory forecasting at urban intersections is often studied assuming that reliable bird's-eye-view (BEV) motion histories are available, which in practice requires costly resources such as LiDAR, aerial views, HD maps, or calibrated infrastructure. We address this upstream perception-to-forecasting problem by reconstructing and predicting agents' BEV trajectories only from paired opposite-corner RGB cameras mounted on existing urban infrastructure at variable heights at inference time. We introduce the Opposite-Corner Trajectory Reconstruction and Anticipation Architecture (OCTR2A), a modular pipeline integrating per-view detection with class refinement, geometric cross-camera matching, transformer-based BEV projection, and egocentric GR
sa48f07ba41.summary: OCTR2A reconstructs and forecasts bird's-eye-view trajectories at urban intersections using only paired opposite-corner RGB cameras in real time.
sa48f07ba41.why: Shows trajectory forecasting may be possible with existing camera infrastructure instead of costly LiDAR or HD maps.

saa2996a8f6.title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models
saa2996a8f6.description: arXiv:2611.24360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-tuning a vision-language-action (VLA) model on a few dozen demonstrations is the standard way to put a manipulation policy on a robot, yet the resulting policy silently assumes that the camera and the robot base stay exactly where they were during data collection: a bumped tripod or a base re-docked a few centimetres away makes it reach for the wrong place. We show that both failures are one phenomenon, a change of the camera-to-base extrinsic that the policy has memorised, and that the robot carries everything needed to undo it. We introduce WACO, a world-anchored canonicalization framework for VLA models: the arm, placed by forward kinematics at the measured joint angles, serves as a metric calibration target, and the static scene se
saa2996a8f6.summary: Researchers propose a method to make few-shot vision-language-action robot policies robust to shifts in camera-to-base extrinsics after fine-tuning.
saa2996a8f6.why: Addresses a practical failure mode where bumped cameras or re-docked robot bases break learned manipulation policies.

s054e4816bd.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization: Fusing Expert Knowledge with Numerical Data
s054e4816bd.description: arXiv:2611.24377v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (MFBO) reduces engineering design cost by combining inexpensive low-fidelity (LF) models with a few accurate high-fidelity (HF) evaluations and sequentially selecting designs to evaluate. However, when HF data are scarce, the LF-HF discrepancy is difficult to learn from numerical data alone, especially when physics omitted in the LF model makes it design-dependent. Yet even without sufficient data, domain experts often know which physics the LF model omits and under which conditions its effect grows. Existing multi-fidelity (MF) models cannot use such qualitative knowledge directly, but large language models (LLMs) can interpret it and compare designs accordingly. The proposed LLM-Assisted MFBO adds a kn
s054e4816bd.summary: A paper proposes using LLMs to incorporate expert knowledge into multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization when high-fidelity data is scarce.
s054e4816bd.why: Offers a way to use domain expertise to reduce costly simulation runs in engineering design when data is limited.

s6dd5ad536c.title: Enhancing Active Learning Performance with Initial Data Selection Based on Foundation Models
s6dd5ad536c.description: arXiv:2611.24384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In active object detection, selecting the initial labeled pool is essential, especially in complex datasets with expensive labeling and low resource budget. This study presents an active learning framework designed to optimize the initial training cycle of active learning for the object detection task. Our approach diverges from traditional methods by utilizing feature-based clustering from the YOLO-World model and refining images based on objectness scores rather than relying on uncertainty sampling in the initial cycle. This approach focuses on finding samples with various features and emphasizes training in areas where the foundation model is most confident. Doing so helps the model better understand different types of objects. For subse
s6dd5ad536c.summary: A framework uses YOLO-World feature clustering and objectness scores to select a better initial labeled pool for active object detection.
s6dd5ad536c.why: Reduces labeling cost in object detection projects with small budgets by improving the first active learning cycle.

sdebe89d18f.title: Temporal Rank in Recurrent Neural Networks
sdebe89d18f.description: arXiv:2611.24394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are a natural framework for temporal modelling, yet are often dismissed due to their sequential, non-parallelisable computation and difficulty in capturing long-range dependencies, typically attributed to vanishing and exploding gradients. We identify a distinct and under-explored limitation: an information bottleneck induced by rank-constrained hidden state dynamics, which limits the number of independent input directions that can be preserved over time, as reflected in the rank of the input-to-state mapping. We show that this constraint restricts temporal capacity independently of gradient stability. To address this, we introduce structured high-dimensional state dynamics that preserve temporal separabilit
sdebe89d18f.summary: Researchers identify a rank-constrained information bottleneck in RNN hidden state dynamics that limits preservation of input directions over time.
sdebe89d18f.why: Points to an architectural limit on RNN memory that is distinct from vanishing gradients, relevant to sequence model design.

s2012d3951f.title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL
s2012d3951f.description: arXiv:2611.24413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many multi-step off-policy temporal-difference methods handle policy mismatch through products of per-step trace coefficients, leading to a trade-off between variance control and long-horizon signal. The maximum trace length consequently becomes a sensitive hyperparameter. We propose MINT (Meeting-time INdicators for Truncation), which replaces these products with a binary stopping indicator: one until coupled behavior and target trajectories first meet, zero thereafter. At the true value function, the indicator's idempotence yields a variance bound governed by meeting-time survival. For practical implementation, a single sampled action provides a model-free surrogate for the stopping rule, requiring no transition model or mixing-time estim
s2012d3951f.summary: MINT replaces products of trace coefficients in multi-step off-policy RL with a binary meeting-time stopping indicator to control variance.
s2012d3951f.why: Could reduce sensitivity to trace-length hyperparameters in off-policy reinforcement learning, though the text gives limited practical detail.

s082a18620a.title: Keeping Shielded Data-Driven Controllers Safe Under System Evolution via Model Consistency
s082a18620a.description: arXiv:2611.24428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cyber-physical systems (CPS) increasingly contain data-driven controllers, which raise safety concerns given their black-box nature. A common mitigation is to enforce system safety via a shield around the controller, which restricts the inputs based on assumptions about the physical system. However, these assumptions are usually fixed and may become invalid as the system evolves (during development or due to component degradation), possibly leading to unsafe behavior. We address this limitation in a model-driven approach that treats both the data-driven controller and safety shield as first-class models that are integrated into a virtual single underlying model (V-SUM) alongside system models.
