Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusio
sd0717acd77.summary: Researchers present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework using ProtoVAE to encode multi-layer RGBA designs into one shared spatial prototype plus one vector per layer.
sd0717acd77.why: Representation size no longer grows with cumulative layer extent, which could make generative editing of layered graphic designs more efficient.

sdbefb9b7e6.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
sdbefb9b7e6.description: arXiv:2611.26590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. We introduce the Multimodal Concept Lens (MC-Lens), a multimodal Jacobian lens, to study these functions in VLM concept processing. Its vision encoder and language decoder lenses map intermediate states to a shared semantic space defined by the decoder's output vocabulary to compare concept accessibility across modalities. MC-Lens supports internal concept interventions to examine the role of accessed concepts in downstream computat
sdbefb9b7e6.summary: Researchers introduce MC-Lens, a multimodal Jacobian lens, to probe how vision-language models select and integrate concept information in line with global workspace theory.

s84d8563609.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
s84d8563609.description: arXiv:2611.26624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the ga
s84d8563609.summary: PlayCraft is an automated framework in which a vision-based agent plays generated games and uses its play experience to revise them for mastery and engagement.
s84d8563609.why: It shows agents can iteratively test and refine AI-generated products using their own play experience, a pattern applicable to automated design loops.

sa795e46023.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
sa795e46023.description: arXiv:2611.24943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this
sa795e46023.summary: The paper argues that the tempting analogy between LLM generated token count and classical time complexity does not hold, and disproves the hypothesis tested.
sa795e46023.why: Engineers using token count as a cost proxy should be cautious, since the paper finds the analogy to classical time complexity fails.

s16ff4aab8e.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
s16ff4aab8e.description: arXiv:2611.24963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Do standard benchmarks see the architectural differences that matter? We study it with 64 from-scratch pretraining runs of Transformers and three linear-model families at 1.3-8B parameters on 1-2T Nemotron-CC tokens, at a cost of roughly 100k USD per 8B run. In academic-scale pretraining (1.3B parameters, 100B tokens), architectural differences can all but disappear when the models are carefully tuned. Instead, at 1-2T tokens they become measurable: Canon layers, which add local token mixing, consistently improve Transformers, saving about 30% of pretraining tokens for the same MMLU accuracy at 8B. We also introduce GLA5 and GDN2, which improve gated linear attention and Gated DeltaNet with low-rank output gates. Surprisingly, with Canon, t
s16ff4aab8e.summary: A study of 64 from-scratch Transformer and linear-model pretraining runs at 1.3-8B parameters finds Canon layers consistently improve Transformers at 1-2T tokens, saving about 30% compute.
s16ff4aab8e.why: Architectural differences that vanish at academic scale become measurable at trillion-token scale, so benchmark comparisons at small scale may mislead model architecture choices.

sbc5ae8bd09.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
sbc5ae8bd09.description: arXiv:2611.24969v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. Under moderate to aggressive compression ratios, including up to 90%, PRKV achieves competitive task performance against established eviction baselines while reducing peak memory usage with low end-to-end overhead. These r
sbc5ae8bd09.summary: PRKV is a training-free KV cache eviction method that estimates global token importance using Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs.
sbc5ae8bd09.why: It offers a way to cut long-context LLM KV cache memory without modifying the model, a key inference bottleneck.

s7bc95b891a.title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
s7bc95b891a.description: arXiv:2611.24970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. We construct a 200-item bank of lawful and unlawful interview questions, whose legal classification is based on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. We instruct LLMs to select questions from this bank in preparing for job interviews, across a set of various occupations and contexts, and report the fraction of unlawful questions that LLMs select. Evaluation of 18 closed and open-weight LLMs across ~100,00
s7bc95b891a.summary: HireWatch is an evaluation of whether LLMs comply with U.S. employment law by selecting lawful and unlawful interview questions from a 200-item bank.
s7bc95b891a.why: Teams deploying LLMs in hiring pipelines face legal compliance risk that standard evaluations do not measure.

s6a52661ada.title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
s6a52661ada.description: arXiv:2611.24971v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. However, these gains are not free: in practical deployments, longer prompts directly increase inference cost and latency. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. While prior work has often focused on how many examples to include in ICL, we study the complementary question of whether the available budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or on a larger number of shorter ones. We study this aspect in question answering (QA), by organizing candidate demonstrations into length-based bins and constructing prompts from examples within the same length range unde
s6a52661ada.summary: The paper studies whether a fixed in-context learning token budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or many shorter ones.
s6a52661ada.why: Prompt construction under token budgets directly affects inference cost and latency, which matters for production deployments.

s2789a3dd3f.title: No-Harm-Jury A Jury-Based Multi-Dimensional Harm Evaluation Framework for Medical AI Responses
s2789a3dd3f.description: arXiv:2611.24972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present No-Harm-Jury, a jury-based automated evaluation framework that scores AI-generated medical responses across seven conceptually distinct harm dimensions using a panel of five diverse language models as independent jurors. Responses generated by Ministral-14B on 3,000 questions drawn from PubMedQA, MedQA, and MedMCQA are scored by five jurors across dimensions of informational, social, psychological, autonomy, economic, privacy, and epistemic harm; the 151 empty responses (98 MedQA, 53 MedM- CQA) are excluded, leaving 2,849 valid samples. The median aggregation robustly suppresses individual juror biases while maintaining coverage through complementary specialisation. No existing system combines all five prop- erties of No-Harm-Jur
s2789a3dd3f.summary: No-Harm-Jury is a jury-based framework that scores AI medical responses across seven harm dimensions, using five language models as independent jurors on 3,000 questions.
s2789a3dd3f.why: It offers a multi-dimensional automated method for evaluating harm in medical AI outputs, though its reliability beyond this setup is not established here.

s21ca88d459.title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents
s21ca88d459.description: arXiv:2611.24977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present CANDID (Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution), an execution-control framework designed to enhance the reliability of local computer-use agents (CUAs) in resource-constrained settings. While local CUAs feature robust baseline proficiency in single-step action prediction, they frequently fail at critical junctions due to rigid action loops or premature DONE decisions. Rather than imposing imprecise cognitive loads through textual reflection, CANDID repurposes parallel test-time scaling into a disciplined, execution-level intervention at sparse, failure-prone points. We introduce a loop-recovery mechanism to filter candidates away from repeated behaviors and a conservative, unanimous DONE gating policy that requir
s21ca88d459.summary: CANDID is an execution-control framework that aims to improve reliability of local computer-use agents in resource-constrained settings by addressing rigid action loops and premature DONE decisions.
s21ca88d459.why: It targets known failure modes of local computer-use agents, relevant to teams running agents on limited hardware.

s89760b18fe.title: Trace2ST: Recovering PLC Structured Text from I/O Traces with LLM Generation and Verification
s89760b18fe.description: arXiv:2611.24979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable logic controllers (PLCs), the industrial computers that operate power and process plants, often run programs whose source code is no longer available; however, every input and output of the controller is logged continuously. This paper therefore asks whether a large language model (LLM) can recover an executable program in Structured Text (ST), the standard PLC language of IEC 61131-3, from such input/output records (traces) alone and, equally important, how the recovered program can be verified. To answer this question, we build a generate-replay-feedback pipeline. First, the LLM writes a candidate program from a compressed summary of the trace, without ever seeing the original program. The candidate is then executed one contr
s89760b18fe.summary: Trace2ST studies whether an LLM can recover executable IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PLC programs from logged input/output traces, with a verification approach.
s89760b18fe.why: Recovering lost PLC source code from I/O logs could help industrial teams maintain legacy control systems, though the verification results are not described here.

sf8c01d79a1.title: DL101 The Representation Capability of Neural Network Models
sf8c01d79a1.description: arXiv:2611.24980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universal approximation theorems (Cybenko, Funahashi, Hornik & Leshno) provide the mathematical justification for why neural networks are powerful enough to model complex, nonlinear phenomena. Shallow networks can approximate any continuous function on compact sets. Leshno's theorem clarified that non-polynomial activations are necessary for universality, which explains why ReLU, logistic, hyperbolic tangent, and other common activations work (but pure polynomials do not). However, approximation theorems provide no efficiency, training, nor generalization guarantees. They do not indicate how many neurons are needed for a given accuracy, whether gradient descent will find the right parameters, or whether networks trained on finite data will
sf8c01d79a1.summary: A tutorial explains the representation capability of neural networks, covering universal approximation theorems and the role of non-polynomial activations.

s138a3ed9e0.title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
s138a3ed9e0.description: arXiv:2611.24994v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Here we show that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals. Using a natural-language autoencoder, we translate the activations of a multimodal LLM (Gemma-3-27B) into text and let an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state (the thoughts channel) and the model's answer separately. Across two clinical attack objectives (omitting a pathology, covertly recommending a drug), two input modalities, and two delivery mechanisms, the thoughts channel caught the injection significantly more often than the
s138a3ed9e0.summary: Researchers use a natural-language autoencoder to translate Gemma-3-27B activations into text, letting a judge read the model's verbalized internal state to detect manipulations hidden in answers.
s138a3ed9e0.why: Monitoring internal verbalized states may catch manipulated clinical LLM outputs that look ordinary, a safety approach beyond input and output filtering.

sb2f70a7336.title: On the Impact of Feature Reduction Techniques on Adversarial Attacks
sb2f70a7336.description: arXiv:2611.25004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adversarial attacks have posed significant threats to machine learning models by exploiting their inherent vulnerabilities. Researchers have established an interdisciplinary field called adversarial machine learning to explore these vulnerabilities and develop corresponding defense strategies. Feature reduction strategies are used to decrease the dimensionality of the data in order to reduce training time, avoid the curse of dimensionality, prevent overfitting, and mitigate redundant features. However, their effect on adversarial robustness across different classifiers and attack scenarios remains insufficiently explored. This study aims to analyze the effect of feature reduction techniques on the adversarial robustness of a diverse set of
sb2f70a7336.summary: The paper examines how feature reduction techniques affect the adversarial robustness of machine learning models against adversarial attacks.
sb2f70a7336.why: Dimensionality reduction used for efficiency may change model vulnerability to attacks, a factor to consider in secured ML pipelines.

sfc507974ac.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
sfc507974ac.description: arXiv:2611.25011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way. The sample compression conjecture of Floyd and Warmuth (1995) asserts that every binary concept class of VC dimension $d$ admits a sample compression scheme of size $O(d)$; a weaker conjecture asks only for size polynomial in $d$. Both have remained open: the first bound depending on
sfc507974ac.summary: The paper presents near-quadratic sample compression schemes for all VC classes, addressing the long-open Floyd and Warmuth sample compression conjecture.

s5f27fb5aeb.title: DVBench: End-to-End Benchmark for Real-World UVM Design Verification Agents
s5f27fb5aeb.description: arXiv:2611.25066v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Design verification (DV) remains a major bottleneck in hardware development, with large-scale verification using the Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) being highly labor-intensive. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and agentic systems offer new opportunities for DV automation. However, existing benchmarks primarily construct mutually decoupled subtasks, which deviates from the real-world workflow. In this paper, we present DVBench, the first end-to-end benchmark for Real-World UVM design verification agents. DVBench comprises 95 tasks across 9 functional domains and 5 difficulty levels, covering diverse verification scenarios and design scales. Each task requires agents to independently complete the full verification wo
s5f27fb5aeb.summary: Researchers introduce DVBench, an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating agents that perform UVM hardware design verification in realistic workflows.
s5f27fb5aeb.why: Engineers automating chip verification get a workflow-level benchmark rather than isolated subtask tests, which better reflects real verification effort.

sedd00b491e.title: VisAlloc: Allocating Visual Supervision for On-Policy Self-Distillation
sedd00b491e.description: arXiv:2611.25069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) offers a promising approach to improving visual reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, not all samples benefit equally from privileged visual guidance, and uniform token supervision can dilute visually grounded signals. We propose VisAlloc, a dual-level framework combining sample-level visual filtering with token-level counterfactual reweighting. A fixed paired-teacher filter retains samples answered correctly from an evidence-centered positive crop but incorrectly from a spatially displaced negative crop. At the token level, both EMA teachers score the same student-generated response, and their absolute log-probability differences measure view sensitivity. Additional supervision t
sedd00b491e.summary: VisAlloc proposes a dual-level method for on-policy self-distillation in multimodal LLMs, filtering samples and reweighting tokens to focus on visually grounded supervision.
sedd00b491e.why: It offers a training technique for improving visual reasoning in multimodal models by avoiding diluted supervision signals.

sdef63a3cd0.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
sdef63a3cd0.description: arXiv:2611.25071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval and tools fetch evidence, Mistral-7B writes a cited answer, a code validator checks that cited IDs exist and that numbers match computed notes, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server exposes the pipeline. In live experiments, Laya routed better than
sdef63a3cd0.summary: FinVeriQA is an open-source multi-agent prototype for financial question answering over SEC filings and live market data, where Python computes numbers and a model writes cited answers.
sdef63a3cd0.why: It shows an architecture separating routing, computation, retrieval and verification to reduce LLM numeric errors in financial analysis.

s25eee472f0.title: Living off the Local Model: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
s25eee472f0.description: arXiv:2611.25086v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Browsers now ship local language models to ordinary endpoints. Google includes Gemini Nano in Chrome to enable productivity features such as summarization, with inference running entirely on the device. These browser-embedded models provide new living-off-the-land opportunities for attackers, each instance a potential post-exploitation engine already installed, signed by the vendor, and invisible to network monitoring. The Gemini model is multimodal, capable of processing files, analyzing screenshots, or conversing with an attacker. We show that it can be driven from the host using only interpreters that ship with the operating system and find that the one-time user-activation check before the model is downloaded is easily satisfied with a
s25eee472f0.summary: Researchers show that browser-embedded local language models, such as Gemini Nano in Chrome, can be abused by attackers as post-exploitation engines on endpoints.
s25eee472f0.why: Security teams must consider on-device browser AI as a new attack surface that evades network monitoring and is vendor-signed.

s3dae92b55a.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
s3dae92b55a.description: arXiv:2611.25105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentag
s3dae92b55a.summary: MAWAM is a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates future views and action chunks for coordinated manipulation across multiple robots.
s3dae92b55a.why: It presents a method for coordinating multi-robot manipulation by predicting team actions and their physical outcomes together.

s210c147935.title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
s210c147935.description: arXiv:2611.25123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval ind
s210c147935.summary: GrepMem is an index-free, lossless memory mechanism for long-horizon LLM agents that avoids summarization by retrieving stored context via search.
s210c147935.why: Agent builders facing context window limits get an alternative to lossy summarization that keeps details available for later tasks.

s92aaae3221.title: CRAFT: Constrained Route planning with Adaptive Framework and Template-based code generation
s92aaae3221.description: arXiv:2611.25128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Everyday routing requests are rarely a point-to-point shortest path. A driver may need to visit stops, sometimes in a fixed order, under time budgets or distance limits, and perhaps recharge their EV car along the way. Each combination is a distinct routing problem that classically requires its own algorithm, so no fixed solver covers the space of queries users may ask. This paper presents CRAFT, which takes a constrained routing query as free text and returns a route that satisfies the user's requirements on a real road network. An LLM parses the query and generates four search functions, which a generic graph-search engine executes on the road network. We formalize the underlying problem as State-Expanded RCSP (SE-RCSP), which extends res
s92aaae3221.summary: CRAFT parses free-text constrained routing queries with an LLM and generates template-based code to return routes meeting requirements on real road networks.
s92aaae3221.why: It shows how LLMs can translate varied user routing requests into solver code instead of relying on one fixed algorithm.

sd36c83e667.title: Game-Theoretic Data Allocation for Expert Specialization and Routing
sd36c83e667.description: arXiv:2611.25167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can the allocation used to train experts also predict which expert will perform best on a prompt? Such a connection would make the intended division of labor inspectable before training and allow the allocation itself to guide inference. We introduce InflEns, a mixture of LoRA experts whose training weights and inference routes come from the same location game in a fixed prompt-trait space. Players choose positions to maximize their expected shares of the prompt distribution, without using expert losses. We utilize the game's kernel-general theoretical criterion for when co-located positions become locally unstable to separation. We evaluate InflEns on a corpus assembled from seven safety-related benchmarks, which demonstrates that the high
sd36c83e667.summary: InflEns is a mixture of LoRA experts whose training data allocation and inference routing both derive from a location game in a prompt-trait space.
sd36c83e667.why: It proposes making expert specialization inspectable before training and using the same allocation to route at inference.

s72b9e664c6.title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models
s72b9e664c6.description: arXiv:2611.25170v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An observable decision reveals the selected action but does not determine which alternatives were internally represented. Drawing on prospection research and hippocampal forward-sweep observations, we develop Before the Choice, an evidence-oriented framework distinguishing future-directed content, prospective computation, and causal guidance. The framework organizes four experimental contrasts and makes their alternative explanations explicit. Its first test case concerns unchosen trajectories in deterministic symbolic environments. A preregistered low-rank probe evaluated once on a sealed TEST did not meet its criterion (paired accuracy 0.020 versus 0.195 for a text-and-observed-choice baseline; 293 admissible pairs). Exploratory H1b expos
s72b9e664c6.summary: The Before the Choice paper presents an evidential framework for testing whether language models internally represent unchosen alternatives before deciding.

scc8d8ff4bb.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
scc8d8ff4bb.description: arXiv:2611.25191v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. In 814 RL runs that teach 7-8B models to answer closed-book questions or abstain, we ask what passes. What a grader knows about single answers stays home. A wrong answer that a judge rewards is memorised for that one question. A model trained with the answer key, or with a far stronger judge, chooses which new questions to answer no better than the untrained model does by sampling 32 answers and abstaining where they disagree; the grader's knowledge adds about one corrected answer per hundred questions. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. A judge that rejects eleven of the twelve correct training answers
scc8d8ff4bb.summary: A study of 814 RL runs finds that knowledge from an LLM judge used as reward stays largely specific to individual answers and does not transfer to choosing new questions to answer.
scc8d8ff4bb.why: Teams using LLM judges as RL rewards should not assume the judge's knowledge transfers to the trained model's broader behavior.

s1ad85ac116.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
s1ad85ac116.description: arXiv:2611.25194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn
s1ad85ac116.summary: MADJEPA is a medical anomaly detector that uses a multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture trained only on healthy patient images.

s282cfb25ff.title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions
s282cfb25ff.description: arXiv:2611.25199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts. Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects. Recent methods that instead exploit explicit spatial information are typically limited to coarse corrections, missing the nuanced, task-relevant motion most manipulation tasks require. We propose VG-Steer, which corrects existing polici
s282cfb25ff.summary: VG-Steer proposes test-time adaptation for frozen robot policies, correcting actions using visual-geometric abstractions aligned in context rather than signals learned from robot datasets.
s282cfb25ff.why: It offers a way to adapt robot policies to out-of-distribution settings with limited real-world data.

s99be32b1b9.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
s99be32b1b9.description: arXiv:2611.25209v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it. Data can satisfy the FAIR principles and still mislead a machine acting alone. We propose that Earth-science data become AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled), an agent-specific requirements layer that extends FAIR, within a three-part agenda: AWARE data, bounded tools, layered validation. The ingredients exist across community infrastructure. We outline a staged, measurable path to adoption, intended to reduce silent error.
s99be32b1b9.summary: The paper proposes AWARE, an agent-specific data readiness layer extending FAIR principles for Earth-science data used by autonomous AI agents.
s99be32b1b9.why: Data teams building agents on scientific datasets need requirements beyond FAIR, since agents cannot supply expert judgement.

sa3a7dd4cbd.title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
sa3a7dd4cbd.description: arXiv:2611.25215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and produci
sa3a7dd4cbd.summary: ROAM is a system combining a vision-language model with learned locomotion so legged robots can perform kilometer-scale navigation in alpine and urban settings.
sa3a7dd4cbd.why: It demonstrates integrating VLM reasoning with low-level control for long-range robot navigation in unstructured environments.

s7dc0b6c014.title: Reject and Report: Forgery-Evident Undetectable Watermarks for Generative Image Models
s7dc0b6c014.description: arXiv:2611.25226v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Provenance schemes such as those based on content watermarks let images from a generative model be traced back to it. A practical watermarking scheme must be accurate at a low false-positive rate (FPR), robust under content-preserving processing, and undetectable. In addition, it must resist forgery; otherwise, even from a single watermarked image and a surrogate model, an adversary can imprint the watermark onto an arbitrary image or regenerate new content that carries it, falsely attributing harmful content to a model or making authentic photographs appear AI-generated. We argue that a watermarking scheme should not only reject forgeries but also report them: a forgery rejected as unwatermarked leaves no trace of the attempt. State-of-the
s7dc0b6c014.summary: The paper presents forgery-evident undetectable watermarks for generative image models, aiming to detect forged watermarks and reject them rather than accept forged attributions.
s7dc0b6c014.why: Provenance systems for generated images must resist forgery, which affects how platforms attribute harmful or authentic content.

s4e21fa0de8.title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters
s4e21fa0de8.description: arXiv:2611.25235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy
s4e21fa0de8.summary: Researchers study how user memories stored in LLM parameters should persist or decay, arguing memory systems need lifecycle governance rather than indefinite retention.
s4e21fa0de8.why: Suggests parametric memory designs should include forgetting and updating mechanisms, not just continual learning, to stay deployable.

sed96183733.title: Beyond Restoration: Content-Degradation Factor Unfolding for Real-World Concealed Object Segmentation
sed96183733.description: arXiv:2611.25239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable visual perception under degradation requires distinguishing task-relevant content from degradation-induced variations, especially in concealed object segmentation (COS), where foreground cues are inherently weak. The central challenge is not merely improving visibility, but identifying reliable content evidence amid degradation-induced variations. RGB-space segmentation often entangles content and degradation cues, while restoration-based methods primarily focus on image recovery and task interaction. This motivates explicit factorization to distinguish content evidence from degradation effects and assess its reliability. Retinex provides a spatially aligned basis for this separation but remains illumination-centric. We therefore e
sed96183733.summary: Researchers propose explicitly factorizing content from degradation cues to improve concealed object segmentation on real-world degraded images, rather than relying on restoration.

s7989c2a6f0.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
s7989c2a6f0.description: arXiv:2611.25254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these mod
s7989c2a6f0.summary: Researchers present PLANTA, an ontology-based method that jointly adapts robot task plans and architectural configurations during mission planning.
s7989c2a6f0.why: Shows how coupling task planning with architecture reconfiguration may matter for adaptive robotic systems, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s3199791594.title: Keel: A Frontier Model Teaches a Vision-Language Model by Rewriting Its Weights
s3199791594.description: arXiv:2611.25257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a frontier model repair a vision-language model (VLM) by rewriting its weights? Small reasoning VLMs such as Qwen3.5 need such a repair: in thinking mode they fall into loops on many image questions, repeating themselves until the token limit, spending the whole budget and losing the answer. The usual remedies act on the decoding, leaving the looping model as it was, or must be told what to change. Yet the cause is written in the weights. Keel, the first agentic weight-editing method for VLMs on image tasks, finds and removes it there. Told only the symptom, an editor, a frontier multimodal LLM acting as an agent, locates the cause, edits the weights and tests them, with a failure census and instruments showing it the failing images and
s3199791594.summary: Keel, a agentic weight-editing method, uses a frontier model to find and remove looping behavior in a small vision-language model by rewriting its weights.
s3199791594.why: Offers a new way to repair model failure modes directly in weights instead of only adjusting decoding.

s824e342a43.title: When Objectives and Evaluators Disagree: Evaluating Transfer for Post-hoc Demographic Framing Mitigation
s824e342a43.description: arXiv:2611.25258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc rewriting is used to reduce demographic disparities in LLM-generated text when the source model is inaccessible. A rewrite can look successful merely because it improved its own target or satisfied its selector. We study this as a transfer problem on 660 gender pairs and 1,980 age contrasts of demographic-conditioned climate messages. A rewriter proposes edits, a selection model chooses among constraint-satisfying candidates, and an independent evaluator uninvolved in either rates pairwise framing disparity. A fixed policy that always targets the message with the lower Persuasion Bias Index (PBI) transfers inconsistently across axes and outcome aggregations. An adaptive policy that proposes edits on both sides but accepts at most o
s824e342a43.summary: Researchers evaluate post-hoc rewriting to reduce gender and age framing disparities in LLM climate messages, using an independent evaluator to test whether gains transfer.
s824e342a43.why: Shows rewrites can appear successful against their own selectors, so teams need independent evaluators to measure bias mitigation.

sb3e4fb5306.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models
sb3e4fb5306.description: arXiv:2611.25288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern recommendation systems face substantial memory pressure, largely from the sparse embedding layer that maps high-cardinality categorical features into dense vectors. In-training embedding pruning (ITEP) removes less important embedding rows during training, yielding end-to-end memory savings but sometimes degrading accuracy because per-table pruning ratios are set by size-based heuristics. We use feature importance (FI) to guide these ratios (FI-ITEP), assigning higher pruning to tables tied to less important features. Across three large-scale recommendation models, FI-ITEP achieves 20--40% total memory reduction while matching or improving accuracy relative to percentile-based ITEP. Because the feature-importance signal requires mini
sb3e4fb5306.summary: Researchers propose guiding in-training embedding pruning with feature importance to set per-table pruning ratios in large recommendation models.
sb3e4fb5306.why: Could reduce memory use in recommendation systems while avoiding the accuracy losses of size-based pruning heuristics.

s8585bfae02.title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
s8585bfae02.description: arXiv:2611.25289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than
s8585bfae02.summary: Researchers compare black-box and white-box confidence methods for eleven open-weight LLMs used as zero-shot classifiers across five datasets.
s8585bfae02.why: Gives guidance on which confidence signals to trust when using zero-shot LLMs as classifiers in production.

s4ca1bd2307.title: ReLay: Bidirectional Layout-Code Translation and Library Evolution for Reusable and Process-Portable Analog Design
s4ca1bd2307.description: arXiv:2611.25328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. We also introduce the first layout-code benchmark: 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-sourc
s4ca1bd2307.summary: ReLay is a bidirectional framework that recovers generator programs from analog layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs.
s4ca1bd2307.why: Could help analog design teams reuse existing layouts and migrate them across process technologies.

s17e39d347f.title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation
s17e39d347f.description: arXiv:2611.25335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) is increasingly applied to scientific imaging domains, such as microscopy, where labels are scarce but noisy data is abundant. These domains exhibit significant signal-dependent noise, which can create a representational shortcut: since both augmented views derive from the same noisy image, the encoder can boost view agreement by also encoding noise patterns rather than semantic content. To enable noise-robust representation learning without knowledge of underlying noise models, we introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation (SEANA), a drop-in module that generates noise-aware SSL views. SEANA learns an invertible variance-stabilizing transform (VST) from noisy data, then estimates the clean signal and resamples
s17e39d347f.summary: Researchers introduce Self-Aligned Noise Augmentation to stop self-supervised learning from encoding noise patterns instead of semantic content in scientific imaging.
s17e39d347f.why: Relevant for teams training self-supervised models on noisy scientific data where labels are scarce.

sb109a6d979.title: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
sb109a6d979.description: arXiv:2611.25339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As LLM agents increasingly generate RTL alongside the tests and reviews that validate it, self-generated evidence is a weak foundation for trustworthy hardware. We present our seven-stage verification-gated workflow, evolved during a post-quantum design port, in which a gate counts only if shown able to fail on negative controls and fault mutants, and reviewer agents audit work before commit. We then audit this evidence with tool-selected netlist mutants, flaw replays, and formal checks. The flow ported an ML-KEM-768/ML-DSA-65 accelerator to a 300 MHz Zynq UltraScale+ key-custody card: all six operations are byte-exact on the board, and it passes all 85 interface-applicable NIST ACVP cases (of 285) and 484 ML-DSA known answers. However, pas
sb109a6d979.summary: Researchers report a verification-gated LLM agent workflow that ported an ML-KEM/ML-DSA post-quantum accelerator to hardware and audited the resulting evidence with mutants and formal checks.
sb109a6d979.why: Shows self-generated tests and reviews from LLM agents can miss flaws, so hardware teams need independent verification.

s667b660cd2.title: FPGA-GEN: Target-Aware RTL Generation via HLS
s667b660cd2.description: arXiv:2611.25351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Successful C/C++ compilation does not guarantee correct or efficient FPGA hardware after high-level synthesis (HLS). FPGA-GEN is an agentic HLS-C generation workflow that encodes specification, readiness, selection, repair, and admission rules in explicit task contracts and bounded tool-feedback loops for candidate-level decisions. On HLS-Eval, five shared-context outputs per task yield 407/425 (95.8%) public-testbench passes. In a cumulative conversion campaign, FPGA-GEN admits 104/107 (97.2%) HLS-LeVeri designs under held-out co-simulation, Vivado synthesis/fit, and same-RTL evidence. In focused TensorCore screening, selected candidate 3 reports 73.7% fewer CSynth cycles and 14.6% fewer LUTs than generated/composed C0, with 26.7% more DSP
s667b660cd2.summary: FPGA-GEN is an agentic workflow that generates target-aware HLS C code, reporting high pass rates on public testbenches and held-out co-simulation.
s667b660cd2.why: Suggests agentic HLS generation with bounded tool feedback can produce FPGA designs that pass rigorous co-simulation.

sb22ec12381.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation
sb22ec12381.description: arXiv:2611.25361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Argumentation frameworks (AFs) provide explicit, formal mechanisms for representing and resolving conflicts and thus have been incorporated into large language model (LLM) decision-making. The benefits vary and depend on how arguments and their relations are constructed, evaluated, and incorporated into the decision process. {We abstract a workflow consisting of four stages based on existing argumentation-augmented methods} and investigate their design choices over tasks of debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact verification. Our evaluation with recent LLMs shows that existing methods do not consistently improve performance across the considered tasks. Motivated by this observation, we develop two task-specific methods. The f
sb22ec12381.summary: Researchers study task-specific design choices for incorporating argumentation frameworks into LLM decision-making across debate and fact-verification tasks.
sb22ec12381.why: Clarifies that the benefit of argumentation-augmented LLM pipelines depends on how arguments are constructed and evaluated.

s87235c7a31.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation
s87235c7a31.description: arXiv:2611.25400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) enables Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to handle distribution shifts during deployment without source-domain retraining. However, backpropagation-based adaptation incurs heavy memory overhead on resource-constrained robots, whereas zeroth-order (ZO) methods suffer from high estimation variance under limited perturbation budgets. We observe that while ZO estimation enables low-memory adaptation with rapid initial gains, it often stalls or degrades over long-horizon updates due to noisy gradient estimates. To address these limitations, we propose Dune, a zeroth-order optimizer that stabilizes long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations. Specifica
s87235c7a31.summary: Dune is a zeroth-order optimizer with time-conditioned historical error regression for test-time adaptation of vision-language-action robot models under distribution shift.
s87235c7a31.why: Offers a lower-memory adaptation approach for robots, where backpropagation-based updates are costly on constrained hardware.

s1672a31b55.title: FG-GraphBench: Benchmarking and Enhancing Fine-Grained Visual Understanding with Multimodal Scene Graphs
s1672a31b55.description: arXiv:2611.25408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-grained visual understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to recognize small visual entities and understand their relationships. Scene graphs offer a natural way to represent this information, organizing visual entities as nodes and their relationships as edges. However, we identify two challenges: existing scene graph benchmarks provide insufficient coverage of fine-grained entities and the relationships among them, and existing methods for fine-grained visual understanding have yet to effectively leverage such graph-structured information in MLLMs. To address these challenges, we introduce Fine-Grained Multimodal Scene Graph Benchmark (FG-GraphBench) and FiGRA. FG-GraphBench is a benchmark comprising three comple
s1672a31b55.summary: Researchers introduce FG-GraphBench, a benchmark with multimodal scene graphs for evaluating and improving fine-grained visual understanding in multimodal LLMs.

s33e27ad16d.title: SGLayout: Schema-Guided Closed-Loop Refinement for LLM-Driven Parameterized Layout Generation
s33e27ad16d.description: arXiv:2611.25410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential in parameterized layout generation via tool-augmented code synthesis. However, LLMs lack spatial awareness, making one-shot generation unreliable. While layout quality can be evaluated with established techniques, a critical gap remains: geometric-domain evaluation outcomes cannot be directly translated into actionable code-level fixes, trapping iterative refinement in blind refactoring. We propose SGLayout, a self-refining framework that closes this gap via a schema-guided mechanism. Upon code execution, a structured schema captures the correspondence between each code-level instance and its geometric attributes, establishing a bidirectional link between code space and geometry space
s33e27ad16d.summary: SGLayout is a self-refining framework that uses a schema-guided mechanism to turn geometric evaluation results into actionable code fixes for LLM-generated parameterized layouts.
s33e27ad16d.why: Shows a path to making LLM code-generation refinement loops more targeted than blind regeneration.

sf1c3ab95da.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
sf1c3ab95da.description: arXiv:2611.25412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-impact attacks on PHP web applications often chain limited-capability vulnerabilities with other flaws or intended behaviors. Discovering these chains requires identifying flaws and the dependencies enabling capability composition. Existing vulnerability discovery techniques analyze flaws in isolation, while attack planning assumes known components. This separation makes it difficult to discover previously unknown components whose security relevance becomes apparent only through their potential roles in an exploit chain. We present ChainAgent, a goal-directed LLM-agent framework that jointly discovers exploit-chain components and their capability dependencies in source code. Guided by an empirical study of 386 real-world web exploit ch
sf1c3ab95da.summary: ChainAgent is presented as an automated system for discovering chainable vulnerabilities in PHP web applications, combining flaw identification with exploit-chain dependencies.
sf1c3ab95da.why: Chained low-severity flaws can enable high-impact attacks, so automated chain discovery could help security teams find risks that isolated scanning misses.

s9d012a181a.title: Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning for Mammography Vision--Language Models
s9d012a181a.description: arXiv:2611.25418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical vision--language models (VLMs) often need to identify small, subtle lesions within high-resolution images containing extensive normal anatomy and redundant visual information. Visual-token compression improves efficiency, but preserving salient regions alone can discard the context needed for diagnostic interpretation. This context can extend across images: in bilateral mammography, the opposite breast provides a patient-specific anatomical reference. Yet retaining such evidence does not ensure that the model uses it effectively. We propose Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning (BESR), which connects evidence preservation with comparative assessment through a bilateral-guided token selector and a bilateral reward. Under a share
s9d012a181a.summary: Researchers propose a bilateral evidence selection method for mammography vision-language models that uses the opposite breast as a reference for diagnosis.

s3b225ecfb8.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
s3b225ecfb8.description: arXiv:2611.25429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent skills package procedural knowledge as natural-language instructions, and a skill helps only when its instructions are correct and properly followed by the agent. Self-evolving agents revise their own skills from the runs they make, but existing methods judge each run as a whole, by its outcome or by where it went wrong, and cannot tell whether a failure comes from a wrong instruction or from one the agent did not follow. Instruction-level coverage was introduced to test skills and labels each instruction of a run as follow, not-follow, or not covered, which separates these causes. We leverage it for skill self-evolution with SkillPlumber, a framework in which an agent evolves its own skills where coverage shows they fall short. A per
s3b225ecfb8.summary: Researchers propose coverage-guided self-evolution for agent skills, labeling each instruction in a run as followed, not followed, or otherwise to revise skills.
s3b225ecfb8.why: Distinguishing wrong instructions from instructions the agent failed to follow could make self-improving agent skills more reliable to maintain.

sf9a33d8778.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
sf9a33d8778.description: arXiv:2611.25436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort. Our key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient candidate coverage from excessive deep expansion, and these conditions require different allocation decisions. Raptor therefore extracts complementary rejection-aware signals to characterize speculative progress, f
sf9a33d8778.summary: Raptor is a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to adapt tree-based speculative decoding for vision-language models with long visual contexts.
sf9a33d8778.why: Faster VLM inference with long visual inputs could lower serving costs, though the text gives no benchmark results.

sc2f91161c9.title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation
sc2f91161c9.description: arXiv:2611.25462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hierarchical reinforcement learning enables sequential tasks to be represented as compositions of separately trained skills. This paper evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation, comparing their training requirements and task performance with flat reinforcement learning baselines. The evaluation concerns complete pipelines with task-specific observation, reward and control structures. In navigation, two parameterised skills are reused across unseen FourRooms layouts under manually specified high-level plans. In manipulation, reaching, grasp alignment and lifting are trained separately, with downstream skills initialised from states collected during predecessor rollouts. Across unsee
sc2f91161c9.summary: A study evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical reinforcement learning pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation against flat RL baselines.

s7bcc70a701.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
s7bcc70a701.description: arXiv:2611.25469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An image can pass automated safety checks while showing harmful content to its human viewer. We introduce DRJanus, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display. Automated systems often read only an image's SDR base, whereas HDR viewers reconstruct its appearance using an auxiliary gain map. DRJanus inverts this reconstruction to embed two independently chosen color images in a single JPEG, without querying or optimizing against the target model. It preserves the chosen SDR base exactly and reconstructs HDR targets at an average PSNR of 43.03 dB across 400 images. On a benchmark of 100 sexual-content images, DRJanus evades detection by all six tested com
s7bcc70a701.summary: DRJanus is a visual camouflage attack that embeds two images in one JPEG, so automated checks see benign SDR content while HDR viewers see harmful content.
s7bcc70a701.why: Content moderation pipelines that read only SDR bases can be bypassed, so teams running image safety checks should account for HDR gain maps.

sca75aaf74d.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins
sca75aaf74d.description: arXiv:2611.25471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-based digital twins of air conditioning, a principal energy consumer in manufacturing and buildings, can be generated automatically from a declarative specification of its equipment, connections, and sizing. Large language models (LLMs) now write such specifications from plain-language descriptions. Evaluations of these specifications stop at parse success, completed runs, or textual similarity, and cannot reject a model that converges in simulation but is physically wrong. In this study, a four-level protocol is proposed that tests whether an LLM-written specification not only executes but also yields a physically valid digital twin. Each specification is executed through static validity, model build, simulation convergence, and be
sca75aaf74d.summary: A four-level executable validation protocol is proposed to test LLM-generated topology specifications for physics-based HVAC digital twins beyond parse success.
sca75aaf74d.why: Simulation convergence alone does not show physical correctness, so engineers using LLM-generated digital twin specs need stronger validation.

se380e40095.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
se380e40095.description: arXiv:2611.25476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks encode learned capabilities in their weights, yet extending those capabilities with explicit task knowledge remains a fundamental challenge. Here we show that Weight-Space Programming (WSP), in which executable programs read, construct or modify a network's weights directly, can install new capabilities within trained neural networks. WeightCode, a WSP framework, uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks using task knowledge and their existing weights, without gradient-based training. Once installed, the new capabilities run independently of the language model. Given a grammar or eight demonstrations, weight programs enable previously unseen co
se380e40095.summary: WeightCode uses a frozen language model to write executable weight programs that install new computations into trained neural networks via weight-space programming.

s617b4bd409.title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
s617b4bd409.description: arXiv:2611.25477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: BraTS-GoAT Task 3 evaluates brain-tumor segmentation across heterogeneous entities using shared ET, TC, and WT regions. We present a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels, a training-only nested-region objective, and a four-expert bottleneck adapter. Five-fold ResEnc-M/L teachers gener ated predictions for 1,138 unlabeled cases; fusion, hierarchy enforcement, and confidence-and-agreement screening retained 983 for training with 1,351 annotated cases. The final five-fold ResEnc-M entry achieved mean DSC 0.834, mean NSD 0.510, and Acalc = 0.6720 on the validation server. Component effects were modest and region-dependent, with the clearest gains on ET. Source code is available at https://github.com/Hee
s617b4bd409.summary: AIstatLab describes a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet for BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3 brain-tumor segmentation, trained with quality-controlled consensus pseudo-labels and a four-expert adapter.

s1d9e66af52.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan
s1d9e66af52.description: arXiv:2611.25484v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For each fixed $k$, iterative-width search finds optimal plans in polynomial time on tasks of bounded tuple-chain width, but the approximability of planning width has remained open even when an optimal plan is supplied. When all optimal plans visit the same state sequence, we characterize set and chain width as hitting numbers of competing states. We construct positive-precondition STRIPS tasks with a supplied unique optimal plan, a single reachable goal state, binary branching, and constant-size actions. Every reachable state lies on a goal-reaching execution at most one action longer than optimal, yet distinguishing width $1$ from $\Theta(N)$, where $N$ is the number of atoms, is NP-hard for set, chain, and goal-admissible width. Unless $
s1d9e66af52.summary: A paper proves that planning width is hard to approximate even when a unique optimal plan is supplied, for positive-precondition STRIPS tasks.

s818f31cc51.title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations
s818f31cc51.description: arXiv:2611.25503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech-scene generation aims to synthesize intelligible target speech together with diverse environmental sounds as a coherent acoustic scene. The task is considered challenging in two respects. Speech and environmental audio differ substantially in their semantic and acoustic characteristics, yet existing approaches typically model the complete scene using a single mixed acoustic representation. At the same time, the two sounds are closely related in real-world speech scenes, whereas conventional approaches usually rely on simulated scenes mixed from independently recorded sources. We propose a large language model (LLM)-based framework for joint modeling of distinct speech and environment token streams. A source-aware neural audio codec e
s818f31cc51.summary: Researchers present a joint language modeling approach for speech-scene generation that uses distinct token representations for speech and environmental sounds.

s8c7cb4003b.title: Persona Lenses: What Makes a Vision-Language Model See Through Its Persona's Eyes?
s8c7cb4003b.description: arXiv:2611.25508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models have been used to simulate where a user looks on a web page. However, a persona in the prompt reaches the simulated gaze only partly. We measure this reach as the difference in one model's gaze between two MatrAIx personas that differ in a single attribute. We introduce persona lenses, which place the persona between the model and the page: a text lens (a two-step prompt in which the model first writes what the persona would look at), a pixel lens (marks on the region matching the persona's interests) and a weight lens (a dwell reward gated to keep the scanpath natural). Using Qwen3-VL (4B and 32B) and Qwen3.5-9B on generated and live pages, we compare the lenses with one another and with scale, the 32B model with no
s8c7cb4003b.summary: Persona lenses are introduced to test how much a persona in the prompt affects a vision-language model's simulated gaze on web pages, using text, pixel, and weight lenses.
s8c7cb4003b.why: Measuring how persona prompts shape VLM outputs matters for teams using simulated user attention in UX or ad testing.

s6a41ba8706.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
s6a41ba8706.description: arXiv:2611.25526v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. Runtime Guardrail (RG) maps this record to an allow, block, or user-approval decision; Predefined Task Routing (PTR) serves recurring requests through verified routes with post-execution screen checks; and a floating interface keeps execution in a compact overlay. On MobileSafetyBench, MAT
s6a41ba8706.summary: MATE is an execution-layer system that sits between mobile agent action proposals and device effects, using a runtime guardrail to allow, block, or request user approval.
s6a41ba8706.why: Mobile agents touching payments, settings, and private data need enforcement outside the model, and this architecture shows one way to build that boundary.

sc89424b5a2.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
sc89424b5a2.description: arXiv:2611.25527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A recommendation page is consumed as a whole: the items on it compete for attention and complement one another, so the best page is not simply the individually best items placed side by side. We study whole-page optimization, which selects and orders the items on a page jointly to maximize the score of the page. The number of possible pages grows combinatorially, so good pages must be generated rather than enumerated. Some generative re-ranking methods use the same page-level training signal for every choice in a sampled page. Others imitate target pages built before training, which remain largely fixed as the generator improves. We address both limitations with one local page-level objective, which repeatedly moves the current generator to
sc89424b5a2.summary: Researchers study generative ranking policies for whole-page optimization, selecting and ordering recommendation items jointly to maximize page-level score.

s692dd72e45.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
s692dd72e45.description: arXiv:2611.25529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to f
s692dd72e45.summary: CoachSI is a robot policy self-improvement method in which a frozen vision-language model coaches the policy in language to supply missing next steps in long-horizon tasks.
s692dd72e45.why: Language-based coaching from a frozen VLM offers a way to improve robot policies without new skill demonstrations, relevant to robotics teams.

s670a117ee6.title: Towards Autoregressive Neural Network Parameter Generation
s670a117ee6.description: arXiv:2611.25538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently established a new paradigm in machine learning, demonstrating exceptional zero-shot generalization and complex reasoning capabilities. Concurrently, neural network parameter generation has emerged as a promising avenue for rapid task adaptation and model synthesis. Existing weight generation techniques, however, struggle to jointly learn the distribution of diverse models, to encode heterogeneous architectures within a single generator, and to generalize out of distribution. We therefore ask whether pretrained parameters can be encoded into a discrete domain so that the zero-shot generalization LLMs exhibit in text generation can be transferred to weight generation. Following this view, we propose
s670a117ee6.summary: Researchers study autoregressive neural network parameter generation, aiming to learn distributions over diverse architectures and generalize out of distribution.
s670a117ee6.why: Could enable faster task adaptation by generating model weights, but the description only outlines the problem and motivation.

s898898b4ab.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction
s898898b4ab.description: arXiv:2611.25557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task-specific rubrics are increasingly used to evaluate open-ended language-model outputs, yet constructing comprehensive evaluation criteria from complex source documents remains challenging. We study automatic rubric construction in professional mergers and acquisitions (M&A) due diligence, where evaluation criteria must be inferred from task instructions and supporting documents without access to an expert-authored reference rubric. We introduce a multi-axis generation framework that explores complementary structural and free-form views of the source evidence to construct a broad pool of candidate evaluation criteria. To distinguish failures of criterion discovery from failures of candidate selection, we introduce the coverage-selection
s898898b4ab.summary: A paper finds that ranking, rather than generation, is the main bottleneck limiting LLM-built evaluation rubrics for M&A due diligence tasks.
s898898b4ab.why: Suggests teams building LLM evaluation rubrics should focus on selecting criteria, not only generating more candidates.

sb7d196b223.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video
sb7d196b223.description: arXiv:2611.25567v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the
sb7d196b223.summary: Researchers propose an online, instruction-conditioned method to detect mistakes in egocentric procedural videos as the video unfolds.
sb7d196b223.why: Relevant to building real-time assistants that flag procedural errors while there is still time to recover.

s38e21e3365.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
s38e21e3365.description: arXiv:2611.25580v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scal
s38e21e3365.summary: FlashX proposes reusing robotic experiences stored in CBA-based NAND flash to warm-start diffusion-based denoising for embodied agents.
s38e21e3365.why: Points to hardware-level storage for experience reuse, which could cut compute for robot policies in unfamiliar environments.

s8e2654b2a1.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
s8e2654b2a1.description: arXiv:2611.25582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a well-established paradigm for augmenting large language models (LLMs) with information retrieved from external corpora. However, developing effective RAG systems requires substantial engineering effort and iterative experimentation, as effective design choices vary across tasks and domains. With rapid advances in LLM agent capabilities, we ask how well these agents can autonomously build RAG systems and how effectively they can improve them through iteration. In this paper, we propose AutoRAGBench, the first benchmark to evaluate how well LLM agents develop RAG systems from scratch in an open code space. It comprises nine RAG system development tasks. For each task, agents build RAG systems from scr
s8e2654b2a1.summary: AutoRAGBench is introduced as a benchmark measuring how well LLM agents can autonomously build and iteratively improve RAG systems.
s8e2654b2a1.why: Gives engineers a way to measure whether coding agents can handle the iterative engineering work of building RAG pipelines.

s0621fd1c0c.title: An Explainable and Scalable Hierarchical Tensor Framework for Integrating Multi-Omics and Digital Pathomics
s0621fd1c0c.description: arXiv:2611.25584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background: Precision oncology requires integration of heterogeneous molecular and pathology data, yet many fusion models offer limited biologically grounded interpretability and struggle with missing modalities. Methods: We present Hierarchical Interpretable Tensor Fusion (HIT-Fuse), integrating six modalities: somatic copy number variation, DNA methylation, RNA sequencing, microRNA expression, RPPA protein abundance, and vision transformer-derived pathomics across four TCGA cohorts (glioma, lung adenocarcinoma, breast, and kidney cancer).
