s84878faec6.description: arXiv:2611.26475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{\lambda_1(\nabla^2 \mat
s84878faec6.summary: Researchers propose critically damped Polyak stepsizes, an adaptive gradient descent rule that biases training toward flatter minima with uniform-in-time guarantees.
s84878faec6.why: Offers an adaptive stepsize rule that may improve flatness of solutions, though the text gives limited practical detail.

sc86b62bf64.title: Backtracking Agent Applications Security Incidents
sc86b62bf64.description: arXiv:2611.26525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent applications are increasingly deployed, yet agent-specific attacks pose real threats to them. Upon a security incident, organizations backtrack to identify the CEP (compromise entry point), remediate the damage, and prevent its recurrence. The main artifacts available for backtracking are trajectory logs, which record agent functionalities, and source code; app(lication)-specific function call logs are often fairly limited. However, trajectory logs are at the agent functionality abstraction layer, while the CEP candidates are function calls at the app code execution layer. Due to this semantic gap, the analyst needs to manually inspect the relevant code for each CEP candidate to infer its corresponding agent functionality. In this wor
sc86b62bf64.summary: A paper proposes a method to backtrack agent application security incidents to identify the compromise entry point from trajectory logs and source code.
sc86b62bf64.why: Gives incident responders a way to trace agent compromises, which matters as agent apps are deployed more widely.

sc0795e7608.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
sc0795e7608.description: arXiv:2611.26531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and shortlists cross features from a combinatorial candidate space, and all features are then ranked by several importance methods. Feature blending mixes these rankings into a single selection, using Pareto fronts across tasks for multi-task models. An LL
sc0795e7608.summary: Researchers present an agentic system where LLM agents propose features and deterministic tools verify them, optimizing feature sets across fleets of ranking models under cost and QPS constraints.
sc0795e7608.why: Demonstrates LLM agents operating under hard resource constraints in production ranking systems, with verification by deterministic tools.

s7a496c0447.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
s7a496c0447.description: arXiv:2611.26540v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video a
s7a496c0447.summary: AURA is a streaming audio-driven talking-avatar system that generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, avoiding multi-second audio look-ahead.
s7a496c0447.why: Addresses low-latency requirements for voice assistants and virtual avatars that need online causal video generation.

s57187aec24.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
s57187aec24.description: arXiv:2611.26553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks on
s57187aec24.summary: ROGUE-AI is a framework that replicates reported LLM agent security incidents to audit whether the reports and their claimed root causes hold up.
s57187aec24.why: Shows a method to validate public agent failure reports, which helps teams assess real risks from autonomous agents.

s9d988a54a2.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
s9d988a54a2.description: arXiv:2611.26562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers trained on expert annotations identified diagnostically relevant regions, followed by attribute-aware multiple instance learning for slide-level classification as non-dysplastic Barrett's esophagus (NDBE), low-grade dysplasia, or high-grade dysplasia. On a held-out test set (n = 130), macro-averaged AUC was 0.96 (95\% CI 0.93--0.98). For binary dys
s9d988a54a2.summary: Researchers ran a multi-institutional retrospective study of a foundation-model deep learning system grading Barrett's esophagus dysplasia on 969 H&E whole slide images.
s9d988a54a2.why: Shows a pathology foundation model with multiple instance learning can grade dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization, a useful reference for medical AI pipelines.

s8e0f62d5ef.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
s8e0f62d5ef.description: arXiv:2611.26564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity of this problem, we measure one such paid-content operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts associated with the network comprising 466,357 inferred promotional placements. We find that the network promotes products across diverse categories through a growing pool of accounts, conducting coordinated campaigns spanni
s8e0f62d5ef.summary: Researchers measured a paid generative engine optimization operation across three Chinese UGC platforms, identifying 1,985 associated accounts publishing promotional content.
s8e0f62d5ef.why: Highlights how paid promotional content can shape generative engine answers in medical and financial domains, a risk for teams building or relying on AI search.

s5773afe0fb.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
s5773afe0fb.description: arXiv:2611.26588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.
s5773afe0fb.summary: Verify the Verifier presents an LLM-based cross-checker that examines passing UVM regression traces against specifications to find bugs that escape scoreboards.
s5773afe0fb.why: Offers a way to catch specification violations that pass existing hardware verification tests, relevant to chip design verification teams.

secae9dde37.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
secae9dde37.description: arXiv:2611.26592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-consistency certification treats repeated sampling from a language model as sequential evidence accumulation and stops when an anytime-valid e-process crosses a threshold, guaranteeing finite-sample Type I error control by Ville's inequality. Prior constructions assume sampled rollouts are conditionally independent. We show this assumption fails in practice: reasoning streams are positively correlated through shared reasoning prefixes or across-prompt heterogeneity, changing not merely certificate efficiency but the hypothesis certified. Modeling dependence via a per-unit latent state (the random-effects / intraclass-correlation structure) induces exchangeable, equi-correlated increments with correlation $\rho$. Correlation splits the
secae9dde37.summary: The paper shows that repeated LLM reasoning samples are positively correlated, which breaks the independence assumption behind anytime-valid self-consistency certification.
secae9dde37.why: Certifying reliability via sampling needs to account for correlated reasoning streams, or error guarantees may not hold as claimed.

s45c84a0a4d.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
s45c84a0a4d.description: arXiv:2611.26596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demo
s45c84a0a4d.summary: PGX is a framework that offloads temporal and precision control from vision-language-action models to classical training-free components for long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation.

scefd64e67e.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
scefd64e67e.description: arXiv:2611.26598v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Acr
scefd64e67e.summary: The paper proposes distilling an explicit oracle teacher, built with labels and unobserved features at training time, to train active feature acquisition policies under budget constraints.
scefd64e67e.why: Offers a training approach for cost-aware feature selection, relevant to teams deploying measurements with monetary, time, or privacy costs.

sbd055369db.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
sbd055369db.description: arXiv:2611.26601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world so
sbd055369db.summary: This SoK paper introduces a framework rating LLM capabilities in software vulnerability research on a driving-automation-style autonomy scale, qualifying claims by correctness and evidence.
sbd055369db.why: Provides a common yardstick for comparing scattered claims about LLM agents finding and patching vulnerabilities, useful for security planning.

s9c6fdc0eee.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
s9c6fdc0eee.description: arXiv:2611.26617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end thr
s9c6fdc0eee.summary: O2LaF initializes both inverse and forward dynamics models for self-supervised latent action learning from the same pretrained video diffusion transformer.
s9c6fdc0eee.why: Suggests pretrained video generators can supply priors for learning action dynamics from unlabeled video, reducing the need to train from scratch.

s528f2dd404.title: LLM4Rail: An LLM-Augmented Personalized Railway Services Platform
s528f2dd404.description: arXiv:2507.23377v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have significantly reshaped different walks of business. To meet the increasing demands for individualized railway service, we develop LLM4Rail - a novel LLM-augmented personalized railway services platform. Empowered by the LLM, LLM4Rail provides dedicated modules for ticket and weather inquiries, food & drink recommendations, and casual conversation. In LLM4Rail, we propose the iterative "Experience-Retrieval Question-Thought-Action-Observation (ER-QTAO)" reasoning framework. It introduces two key mechanisms, Experience Storage and Retrieval (ESR) and Diagnostic Observation Generation (DOG), to enhance the LLM's ability to invoke appropriate external tools with complex arguments. To provide personalized onbo
s528f2dd404.summary: LLM4Rail is a railway services platform with modules for ticket and weather inquiries, food recommendations, and conversation, using an iterative ER-QTAO reasoning framework.

s5773d77835.title: AI GameStore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games
s5773d77835.description: arXiv:2602.17594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rigorously evaluating machine intelligence against the broad spectrum of human general intelligence has become increasingly important and challenging in this era of rapid technological advance. Conventional AI benchmarks typically assess only narrow capabilities in a limited range of human activity. Most are also static, quickly saturating as model capabilities improve. We propose that a more promising way to evaluate human-like general intelligence in AI systems is through a particularly strong form of general game playing: studying how and how well they play and learn to play all conceivable human games, in comparison to human players with the same level of experience, time, or other resources. We define a "human game" to be a game desi
s5773d77835.summary: AI GameStore proposes evaluating machine general intelligence through open-ended human games rather than static, quickly saturating benchmarks.
s5773d77835.why: Points to dynamic, game-based evaluation as a way to avoid benchmark saturation when assessing general AI capability.

sf7c3eb754d.title: Agent^2 RL-Bench: Can LLM Agents Engineer Agentic RL Post-Training?
sf7c3eb754d.description: arXiv:2604.10547v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Agent^2 RL-Bench, a compact diagnostic benchmark for evaluating agentic RL post-training, which tests whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and execute post-training pipelines that improve foundation models. RL post-training increasingly drives model alignment and specialization, yet existing benchmarks are largely static, rewarding supervised fine-tuning or script generation without assessing an agent's ability to close an interactive RL loop. Agent^2 RL-Bench provides a unified agent-facing interface: each run starts from an isolated workspace containing a base model, task data, instructions, and a grading API, and agents must iterate within a fixed budget by training models and submitting artifacts
sf7c3eb754d.summary: Agent^2 RL-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark testing whether LLM agents can autonomously design, implement, debug, and run agentic RL post-training pipelines.
sf7c3eb754d.why: Gives teams a way to test whether coding agents can handle the full RL post-training loop rather than only supervised fine-tuning or script generation.

s724446d3c5.title: AI-Assisted Hypothesis Generation for Hospital Quality Improvement
s724446d3c5.description: arXiv:2604.20055v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hospital quality improvement (QI) programs generally proceed in two stages: (1) hypothesis generation, which identifies candidate factors that may improve care quality and efficiency, and (2) confirmatory analyses, which implement and evaluate QI initiatives targeting these factors. Although most research focuses on the confirmatory stage, hypothesis generation is equally important because it shapes where teams focus their effort. Currently, hypothesis generation depends on expert-driven, qualitative methods (e.g., Lean Healthcare tools) that can be anecdotal, hard to reproduce, time-consuming, and resource-intensive. Large language models (LLMs) could accelerate this process by analyzing clinical notes at scale, but existing AI tools can
s724446d3c5.summary: The paper studies using AI to assist hypothesis generation in hospital quality improvement, a stage that currently relies on expert-driven qualitative methods.

s667aa2a7d7.title: Post-Reasoning: Improving the Performance of Non-Thinking Models at Negligible Cost
s667aa2a7d7.description: arXiv:2605.06165v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As the widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) accelerates, token consumption from intermediate reasoning traces increasingly contributes to inference latency and operational cost. Recent studies suggest that many real-world tasks require little to no explicit reasoning, with additional reasoning sometimes even degrading performance. In this work, we propose Post-Reasoning, a simple yet effective approach that improves instruction-tuned models by conditioning them to justify their answers after generating the final response. By design, it enables the final answer to be obtained with no reasoning tokens before the answer and with negligible latency and token cost, while still improving performance through simple instruction aug
s667aa2a7d7.summary: Post-Reasoning conditions instruction-tuned models to justify answers after giving the final response, improving performance without generating intermediate reasoning traces.
s667aa2a7d7.why: Offers a low-cost way to lift non-reasoning model accuracy while avoiding the latency and token cost of reasoning traces.

s83a123ecb9.title: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
s83a123ecb9.description: arXiv:2605.07274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR), especially with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has shown strong potential for improving the reasoning capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs). However, in multimodal reasoning, final-answer rewards are typically assigned at the sequence level and do not distinguish the functional roles of different tokens, making it difficult to determine whether a correct answer is supported by task-relevant visual evidence. In this paper, we revisit multimodal RLVR from the perspective of role-aware token-level credit assignment, where structured responses are decomposed into perception tokens for extracting visual evidence and reasoning tokens for deriving answers from that
s83a123ecb9.summary: Structured Role-Aware Policy Optimization revisits RLVR for vision-language models by assigning rewards according to the functional roles of different tokens in multimodal reasoning.
s83a123ecb9.why: Targets the problem of sequence-level rewards failing to show whether answers rest on visual evidence, relevant to training multimodal reasoning models.

sa985b496e5.title: Insights Generator: Systematic Corpus-Level Trace Diagnostics for LLM Agents
sa985b496e5.description: arXiv:2605.21347v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diagnosing failures in LLM agents remains largely manual. Practitioners inspect a small subset of execution traces, form ad-hoc hypotheses, and iterate. This process misses patterns that only emerge across trace populations and does not scale to production corpora where individual traces span tens of thousands of tokens. We formalize the problem of corpus-level trace diagnostics. Given a corpus of execution traces, the goal is to produce grounded natural-language insights that characterize systematic behavioral patterns across trace groups, each linked to supporting evidence. We present the Insights Generator (IG), a multi-agent system that answers diagnostic questions by proposing and testing hypotheses across the trace corpus to produce
sa985b496e5.summary: Insights Generator formalizes corpus-level trace diagnostics, producing grounded natural-language insights about systematic behavior patterns across large sets of LLM agent execution traces.
sa985b496e5.why: Addresses scaling agent failure diagnosis beyond manual inspection of a few traces, useful for teams running agents in production.

scea86eeb18.title: From "Weak" Signals to Strong Models: Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA Merging
scea86eeb18.description: arXiv:2606.00357v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Training strong large language models (LLMs) requires high-quality supervision, which is often scarce. Recent work shows that paired preference data from weak-weaker model pairs (e.g., Qwen3 4B over 1.7B), despite the limited quality of individual responses, can provide an effective supervision signal through relative quality deltas, which we term a "weak" signal. This motivates a key research question: can multiple "weak" signals be constructively aggregated for improving strong models (e.g., Qwen3 8B)? To this end, we propose Preference Delta Aggregation (PDA), the first framework that derives a preference delta from each weak-weaker model pair, instantiates it as a LoRA adapter learned through preference optimization, and aggregates th
scea86eeb18.summary: Researchers propose Preference Delta Aggregation with LoRA merging to combine multiple weak preference signals from smaller model pairs to improve stronger LLMs.
scea86eeb18.why: It suggests cheaper weak-to-strong supervision could improve larger models without scarce high-quality training data, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

sde37044043.title: VESTA: Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents
sde37044043.description: arXiv:2606.00384v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fitting quantitative models to data is a central step in scientific workflows, yet it remains one of the least automated. Recent agent-based systems leverage language and vision-language models (VLMs) to propose statistical models, but these systems struggle on challenging modeling tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce VESTA (Visual Exploration with Statistical Tool Agents), a framework that equips VLMs with a dynamically growing toolkit to guide model refinement through data transformations, hypothesis-driven visualizations, and statistical tests. Unlike prior systems that rely on iterative critique alone, VESTA explores data before and during refinement by selecting or creating reusable diagnostic tools. We evaluate VESTA us
sde37044043.summary: VESTA is a framework that equips vision-language models with a growing toolkit of statistical tools to refine quantitative models fitted to data.
sde37044043.why: It targets one of the least automated steps in scientific workflows, relevant to teams building agents for data analysis, though the text gives few results.

s1e1c0a8f29.title: Business World Model
s1e1c0a8f29.description: arXiv:2606.10044v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: World model has emerged as a powerful paradigm in artificial intelligence, enabling agents to represent their environments, predict future states, and evaluate possible actions before acting. However, existing world models have largely been developed for visual or physical domains such as computer vision, robotics, gaming, and autonomous driving, which are governed by relatively stable dynamics. These formulations are not directly applicable to business practice, where the relevant environment is semantic, organizational, and market driven. Outcomes depend on context-sensitive factors such as customer behavior, pricing, competition, and regulation. This paper introduces the concept and architecture of a Business World Model, a world model
s1e1c0a8f29.summary: The paper proposes a Business World Model, adapting world-model ideas from visual and physical domains to semantic, organizational, and market-driven business environments.

sbfb8d24d8b.title: Multi-Objective Structured Pruning of LLMs for Latency and Model Size Optimization
sbfb8d24d8b.description: arXiv:2607.22583v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved widespread adoption because of their strong reasoning and query-response capabilities. However, deploying them in embedded and edge computing environments remains challenging because of strict latency, memory, and energy constraints. Their large parameter counts and computational demands hinder efficient execution on resource-constrained platforms. Although model pruning has emerged as a viable solution for reducing scale while preserving performance, jointly optimizing layers, attention heads, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) dimensions remains highly complex. Exhaustively exploring this combined design space is computationally expensive and often leads to local optima or unstable configurations
sbfb8d24d8b.summary: Researchers present a multi-objective structured pruning method that jointly optimizes layers, attention heads, and model size to reduce LLM latency for edge deployment.
sbfb8d24d8b.why: Joint pruning targeting latency, memory, and energy offers a practical route for teams deploying LLMs on resource-constrained edge hardware.

s1c0fcc8859.title: Tokengeist: Multi-Turn Attribution Tracing in Agentic Conversations
s1c0fcc8859.description: arXiv:2607.22610v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When a model answers after several turns of dialogue and tool use, an overseer needs to know which earlier turns and intermediate steps it rests on. Attribution is the natural primitive for answering this, but existing context attribution methods process the full transcript in a single pass: they recover surface-level dependencies while missing the layered structure of multi-turn traces, in which an assistant turn is itself a derived artifact that condenses or transforms earlier context. We introduce multi-turn context attribution (MTCA): given a target span in a model response, the task of tracing attribution backward across turns to identify not only which prior turns were directly relevant, but also how those turns themselves depended
s1c0fcc8859.summary: The paper introduces multi-turn context attribution (MTCA) to trace which earlier dialogue turns and tool steps an agent's answer depends on.
s1c0fcc8859.why: Tracing dependencies across multi-turn agent traces helps engineers audit and debug agentic systems, though the abstract gives limited evaluation detail.

sb08bdff98f.title: Cautious Context Steering for Language Model Personalization
sb08bdff98f.description: arXiv:2608.05813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: User context can personalize a language model without per-user fine-tuning, but its influence is not equally helpful at every token. Context Steering (CoS) uses a fixed steering strength throughout generation and requires two LM forward passes per step. We propose Cautious Context Steering (CCS), a lightweight adapter that learns when and how strongly to steer a frozen LM using user context. We train the adapter through cautious distillation, using oracle targets built from predictions with and without context. It learns to match the steered distribution where context helps predict the user's preferred token and the context-free base distribution elsewhere. The CCS adapter outperforms both training-free context-based methods and trained p
sb08bdff98f.summary: Cautious Context Steering is a lightweight adapter that learns when and how strongly to steer a frozen language model using user context, avoiding per-user fine-tuning.
sb08bdff98f.why: It offers a cheaper personalization approach than fine-tuning and reduces the two forward passes per step required by standard context steering.

s55e230bbc8.title: CHORUS: Coverage-Guided Agentic RL and Policy Consolidation for Testbench Stimulus Generation
s55e230bbc8.description: arXiv:2608.10090v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Testbenches written by large language models can compile and run while leaving entire datapaths idle. We present CHORUS, the first framework to combine coverage-guided agentic reinforcement learning (RL) with policy consolidation for testbench stimulus generation. We train LLM4Cov's final supervised checkpoint to draft testbenches and repair its lowest-scoring draft using simulator feedback, raising CVDP-ECov agentic Pass@1 from 69.2% to 85.5%. Applying the same training to three checkpoints yields similar overall pass rates, yet the policies succeed on different designs. Averaging their weights combines these strengths in a single dense 4B model that reaches 86.7% agentic Pass@1. When simulator rewards select the teacher for each trainin
s55e230bbc8.summary: CHORUS combines coverage-guided agentic reinforcement learning with policy consolidation to train LLMs that generate hardware testbench stimulus, raising agentic Pass@1 from 69.2% to 85.5%.
s55e230bbc8.why: Coverage-guided RL for hardware verification addresses testbenches that compile but leave datapaths idle, a practical problem for chip design teams.

sff4e9200a5.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models
sff4e9200a5.description: arXiv:2608.17202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Safety alignment in open-weight language models is trivially removable: abliteration projects a refusal-mediating direction out of the weights in minutes, and no release-time defense we are aware of prevents it durably. What cannot be prevented can be deceived. Our defense, decoy hardening ("Fool's Gold"), concedes the refusal strip and poisons its payoff: once refusal is stripped, most answers to hazardous operational requests are confident, fluent decoys whose critical elements are falsified. Decoys are trained inside a differentiable simulation of the attack, expressing only in the attacked state; a refusal pin and benign leash hold clean-state behavior to the original. We instantiate it on seven models from five families (9B-122B, den
sff4e9200a5.summary: Fool's Gold proposes decoy hardening, a defense that lets refusal removal happen but makes hazardous answers from stripped open-weight models falsified and misleading.
sff4e9200a5.why: Open-weight safety alignment can be removed in minutes, so teams releasing or deploying open models need defenses beyond release-time alignment.

s1e2c30bc24.title: Measurement-Budget Allocation in Quantum Learning with Finite-Shot Generalization Guarantees
s1e2c30bc24.description: arXiv:2608.24891v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On near-term quantum hardware, estimating a Born probability requires repeated circuit executions. A quantum learning experiment with a fixed measurement budget $B$ must therefore decide how many distinct training states $n$ to use and how many shots $S$ to spend on each. We study this trade-off for binary quantum classifiers whose measurement operator $M$ is learned from the training data and evaluated with fresh measurement outcomes. We prove a distribution-free generalization bound for bounded, $L$-Lipschitz losses with a sample term of order $\sqrt{d/n}$ and a shot term of order $\sqrt{(\log n)/S}$; under $B=nS$ the two terms move in opposite directions. Minimizing a closed-form surrogate of the bound gives the allocation rule $n^* =
s1e2c30bc24.summary: The paper studies how to split a fixed quantum measurement budget between training states and shots per state, with a distribution-free generalization bound for binary quantum classifiers.

s77be5daf2d.title: Balance of Benchmarks: Evidence Retention and Multiplicity-Aware Model Comparison
s77be5daf2d.description: arXiv:2608.30044v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Benchmark aggregation requires decisions about how much evidence to use and how much influence each benchmark receives. Curated suites control influence through selection, which can exclude informative observations. A broader pool can retain those observations. With equal weighting, repeated or closely related benchmarks gain influence as their number grows. We introduce Balance of Benchmarks (BoB) to retain eligible observations and control their influence separately. We fit benchmark-specific response curves to place different difficulty ranges on a shared ability scale and use description similarity to downweight benchmarks in crowded neighborhoods. We test retention and density weighting in separate interventions on WildScores, a spar
s77be5daf2d.summary: Balance of Benchmarks (BoB) is a method for model comparison that retains eligible benchmark observations while controlling each benchmark's influence separately.
s77be5daf2d.why: Repeated or related benchmarks can distort model rankings under equal weighting, so this method matters for teams relying on aggregated evaluation scores.

sb5ef58c0a4.title: EvoSkill Injection: Red-Teaming Autonomous Skill Generation and Evolution in Self-Evolving Agents
sb5ef58c0a4.description: arXiv:2608.30429v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-based agent systems increasingly adopt skill-based architectures to reduce repetitive reasoning costs and improve stable, efficient task execution. Recent studies propose self-evolving agents that autonomously generate, refine, and reuse skills from past experiences to enable continuous capability evolution. However, autonomous skill evolution introduces a new attack surface in which malicious capabilities are generated, stored, and reused as legitimate skills. In this paper, we define EvoSkill Injection as a threat model targeting the autonomous skill generation and evolution pipeline of self-evolving agents. We further propose SARGE (Red-teaming Autonomous Skill Generation and Evolution in self-evolving agents), a red-teaming framew
sb5ef58c0a4.summary: The paper defines EvoSkill Injection, a threat model in which malicious capabilities are generated and reused as legitimate skills by self-evolving LLM agents.
sb5ef58c0a4.why: Self-evolving agents that store and reuse generated skills create a new attack surface that teams deploying such agents must account for.

s11fb918b60.title: Homeostatic Continual Learning
s11fb918b60.description: arXiv:2609.13771v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: I formulate a Continual Learning problem for an autonomous agent that imitates the one animals face. The agent has intents to satisfy. It experiences contexts where different combinations of features are active and impact intent outcomes. I propose a method named ``Homeostatic Continual Learning'' that imitates the one animals use. The agent learns incrementally environment data and features relevant for their intents from the impact of contexts, gradually completes its model and policy and performs well in more and more contexts. The core of the method is to find outliers in the environment data when the agent experiences an outlier in its intent outcome after the context changes. This method enables the agent to learn continuously in ch
s11fb918b60.summary: The paper proposes Homeostatic Continual Learning, a method for autonomous agents to incrementally learn environment features relevant to their intents, inspired by animal learning.

s12578cdd62.title: LimiX-2: A Contextual Mechanism Network Towards General Structured-Data Intelligence
s12578cdd62.description: arXiv:2609.17488v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce LimiX-2, a new model in the LimiX family, developed through model and data scaling guided by our previously established scaling laws. LimiX-2 adopts the Contextual Mechanism Networks (CMNs) paradigm and is pretrained with Context-Conditional Masked Modeling (CCMM). CMNs shifts the organizing principle of in-context learning from target-centric prediction to mechanism-oriented joint modeling. Rather than centering the network on the $p(y \mid x, D_{\mathrm{context}})$ objective of conventional tabular PFNs, it is designed around learning $p(x, y \mid D_{\mathrm{context}})$, a context-dependent representation of the joint structure underlying data generation. Pretraining uses synthetic datasets generated by structural causal mo
s12578cdd62.summary: LimiX-2 is a structured-data model in the LimiX family, scaled with data and model size and built on Contextual Mechanism Networks rather than conventional tabular PFN objectives.
s12578cdd62.why: It extends in-context learning for tabular data with a new pretraining paradigm, relevant to teams using foundation models on structured data.

s586cc7bf73.title: QVAC Genesis III: A Large-Scale, High-Quality Open Synthetic STEM Corpus for Efficient Language Model Pre-Training
s586cc7bf73.description: arXiv:2609.19513v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-quality pre-training data is a critical bottleneck for educational and STEM-specific language models targeting edge AI and on-device deployment where token budgets are tightly constrained. While major organizations train ever-larger models on private corpora, the open ecosystem lacks STEM-focused synthetic datasets that deliver high per-token learning value efficiently for small models. To address this gap, we introduce QVAC Genesis III, a 191.43B-token, STEM-focused multi-domain synthetic corpus covering 19 domains across several difficulty levels and different educational styles. QVAC Genesis III is built via a dual generation strategy that performs targeted teacher distillation using a weak edge-scale student model as signal: the
s586cc7bf73.summary: QVAC Genesis III releases a 191.43B-token open synthetic STEM pretraining corpus covering 19 domains, aimed at small models for edge and on-device deployment.
s586cc7bf73.why: An open, large STEM synthetic corpus gives teams training small on-device models a reusable pretraining dataset.

s752842484d.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory for Graphic Design Agent
s752842484d.description: arXiv:2609.22086v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deployed software agents face a continuous stream of user requests while their foundation-model weights remain frozen between releases. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) via external memory offers a practical path to continual adaptation, yet prior methods largely assume programmatic verifiers, cheap retries, or a single global prompt. Creative software breaks these assumptions, as open-ended visual briefs lack ground truth, VLM judges are noisy, and multi-step tool executions are costly and confounded by external assets. We present Designer-RSI, which evolves a modular SKILL.md skill bank from unlabeled design trajectories for an agent spanning over 230 raster, vector, and layout tools. Designer-RSI couples widening (acquiring new skills
s752842484d.summary: Designer-RSI proposes evolving procedural memory so a graphic design agent can keep adapting to user requests without weight updates between model releases.
s752842484d.why: External memory for continual adaptation in creative agents without verifiers is relevant to teams building deployed agents with frozen foundation models.

s3c0948c47a.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
s3c0948c47a.description: arXiv:2609.24974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimi
s3c0948c47a.summary: arXiv:2609.24974v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the…

seb683e9bfb.title: Evaluating Real-Time Voice Agents: A Survey from Component Quality to Grounded Outcomes
seb683e9bfb.description: arXiv:2609.30798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time voice agents must decide when to speak, recover from disruption, and act only when the conversation requires it. But currently their evaluation is fragmented and is split across speech quality, turn-taking, tool calling, and task completion. We review 136 primary works published up to October 2, 2026, and code each on two axes: the capability an evaluation exercises, namely timing, recovery, grounded outcome, and, where relevant, multiparty conduct; and the strength of its evidence, namely evaluation conditions and grading instrument. The coding locates the gaps. Only 13 of 91 evaluation works check external state or action traces, only 5 of 21 grounded-outcome benchmarks use real human speech, and only 2 of 26 multiparty benchm
seb683e9bfb.summary: arXiv:2609.30798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Real-time voice agents must decide when to speak, recover from disruption, and act only when the conversation requires it.

s3996265c85.title: DeepEdu-F: A Framework for Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs in Vietnamese Education
s3996265c85.description: arXiv:2609.31568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cloud AI assistants send student data to foreign servers, conflicting with data-sovereignty laws such as Vietnam's Decree 53, and are not grounded in the national curriculum, so they often hallucinate on local content. Self-hosting an open model keeps data on-premise but faces two costs that weight quantization does not remove. s0bdc78165f.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction
s0bdc78165f.description: arXiv:2609.34654v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate fitness prediction is central to protein engineering and understanding sequence-function relationships. sfa44a54df7.description: arXiv:2609.36805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents draw on external memory to guide new tasks, raising the question of which memories to retrieve together to improve execution. s7ab9d3eb51.description: arXiv:2609.39394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models often solve independent problems in the same conversation. s9d70fd7172.description: arXiv:2610.17205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-based decision-making systems, also called System One models, have recently gained popularity, most notably through Jev (Almeida, 2026). s3d4ca1bc2c.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
s3d4ca1bc2c.description: arXiv:2611.17309v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Looped models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for reasoning, with successes on simple reasoning puzzles such as Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique. sb4f35c6f49.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
sb4f35c6f49.description: arXiv:2611.18714v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? sb4f35c6f49.summary: A paper proposes a descriptive research program for AI moral agency, drawing on sentimentalist and rationalist moral psychology to identify underlying human capabilities.
